title.zh: 卷一百九十九下 列傳第一百四十九下: 北狄
title.raw: 卷一百九十九下 列傳第一百四十九下: 北狄 Volume 199 Biographies 149: Northern Peoples

sentences.zh: 鐵勒 契丹 奚 室韋 靺鞨渤海靺鞨 霫 烏羅渾

translations.literal: Tiele, Khitan, Xi, Shiwei, Mohe, Bohai Mohe, Xi, and Wuluohun.
translations.idiomatic: Tiele, Khitan, Xi, Shiwei, Mohe, Bohai Mohe, Xi, and Wuluohun.

sentences.zh: 鐵勒，本匈奴別種。

translations.literal: The Tiele were originally a separate branch of the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiele were originally a separate branch of the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 自突厥強盛，鐵勒諸郡分散，衆漸寡弱。

translations.literal: From the time the Turks grew powerful, the Tiele tribes were scattered, and their numbers gradually dwindled.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Turks rose to power, the Tiele tribes were scattered and their numbers gradually declined.

sentences.zh: 至武德初，有薛延陀、契苾、回紇、都播、骨利幹、多覽葛、僕骨、拔野古、同羅、渾部、思結、斛薛、奚結、阿跌、白霫等，散在磧北。

translations.literal: By the beginning of the Wude reign, there were the Xueyantuo, Qibi, Huihe, Dubo, Guligan, Duolange, Pugu, Bayegu, Tongluo, Hun, Sijie, Huxue, Xijie, Adie, Baixi, and others, scattered north of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: By the opening years of the Wude era, groups including the Xueyantuo, Qibi, Huihe, Dubo, Guligan, Duolange, Pugu, Bayegu, Tongluo, Hun, Sijie, Huxue, Xijie, Adie, and Baixi were scattered across the lands north of the desert.

sentences.zh: 薛延陀者，自雲本姓薛氏，其先擊滅延陀而有其衆，因號爲薛延陀部。

translations.literal: The Xueyantuo: from Yun their original surname was Xue; their ancestors attacked and destroyed the Yantuo and took their people, and therefore they were called the Xueyantuo tribe.
translations.idiomatic: The Xueyantuo took their name from the Xue clan of Yun. Their forebears had conquered and absorbed the Yantuo people, and from that they came to be known as the Xueyantuo tribe.

sentences.zh: 其官方兵器及風俗，大抵與突厥同。

translations.literal: Their official titles, weapons, and customs were for the most part the same as those of the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Their ranks, arms, and customs were largely the same as those of the Turks.

sentences.zh: 初，大業中，西突厥處羅可汗始強大，鐵勒諸部皆臣之，而處羅徵稅無度，薛延陀等諸部皆怨，處羅大怒，誅其酋帥百餘人。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Daye era, Choru Qaghan of the Western Turks first grew powerful, and all the Tiele tribes submitted to him; but Choru levied taxes without limit, and the Xueyantuo and other tribes all resented him. Choru flew into a rage and executed more than a hundred of their chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Daye reign, Choru Qaghan of the Western Turks first rose to power, and all the Tiele tribes submitted to him. Choru levied taxes without restraint, however, and the Xueyantuo and other tribes grew resentful. Enraged, Choru executed more than a hundred of their chieftains.

sentences.zh: 鐵勒相率而叛，共推契苾哥楞爲易勿真莫賀可汗，居貪汗山北；

translations.literal: The Tiele rose together in revolt and jointly enthroned Qibi Geleng as Yiwuzhen Mohe Qaghan, dwelling north of Tanhan Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: The Tiele rose in revolt together and jointly enthroned Qibi Geleng as Yiwuzhen Mohe Qaghan, with his seat north of Tanhan Mountain;

sentences.zh: 又以薛延陀乙失缽爲也咥小可汗，居燕末山北。

translations.literal: They also made Yishibo of the Xueyantuo Yedie Lesser Qaghan, dwelling north of Yanmo Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: They also installed Yishibo of the Xueyantuo as Yedie Lesser Qaghan, with his seat north of Yanmo Mountain.

sentences.zh: 西突厥射匱可汗強盛，延陀、契苾二部並去可汗之號以臣之。

translations.literal: Shegui Qaghan of the Western Turks grew powerful, and the Yantuo and Qibi tribes both relinquished the title of qaghan and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shegui Qaghan of the Western Turks grew powerful, the Yantuo and Qibi tribes both abandoned the title of qaghan and submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 回紇等六部在郁督軍山者，東屬於始畢，乙失缽所部在金山者，西臣于葉護。

translations.literal: The six tribes including the Huihe at Yudujun Mountain submitted in the east to Shibi; the followers of Yishibo at Jinshan submitted in the west to Yehu.
translations.idiomatic: The six tribes including the Huihe at Yudujun Mountain looked east to Shibi, while the followers of Yishibo at Jinshan looked west to Yehu as their overlord.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年，葉護可汗死，其國大亂。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan, Qaghan Yehu died and his state fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhenguan reign, Qaghan Yehu died and his realm fell into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 乙失缽之孫曰夷男。

translations.literal: Yishibo's grandson was named Yinan.
translations.idiomatic: Yishibo's grandson was named Yinan.

sentences.zh: 率其部落七萬余家附於突厥。

translations.literal: He led his tribe of more than seventy thousand households to submit to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: He led his tribe of more than seventy thousand households to submit to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 遇頡利之政衰，夷男率其徒屬反攻頡利，大破之。

translations.literal: When Jieli's rule declined, Yinan led his followers in a counterattack against Jieli and routed him.
translations.idiomatic: As Jieli's power waned, Yinan led his followers in a counterattack against him and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 於是頡利部諸姓多叛頡利，歸於夷男，共推爲主，夷男不敢當。

translations.literal: Thereupon many clans of Jieli's tribe rebelled against Jieli and went over to Yinan, jointly urging him to be their leader, but Yinan did not dare accept.
translations.idiomatic: Many clans of Jieli's tribe then rebelled against him and went over to Yinan, urging him jointly to become their leader, but Yinan did not dare accept.

sentences.zh: 時太宗方圖頡利，遣遊擊將軍喬師望從間道齎冊書拜夷男爲真珠毗伽可汗，賜以鼓纛。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Taizong was planning against Jieli and sent the raiding general Qiao Shiwang by a secret route with investiture documents to ennoble Yinan as Zhenzhu Pijia Qaghan, granting him drums and banners.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Taizong was plotting against Jieli. He sent the raiding general Qiao Shiwang by a hidden route with investiture documents to ennoble Yinan as Zhenzhu Pijia Qaghan and bestowed upon him drums and banners.

sentences.zh: 夷男大喜，遣使貢方物，復建牙於大漠之北郁督軍山下，在京師西北六千里。

translations.literal: Yinan was greatly pleased, sent envoys to present local products, and again set up his royal camp north of the great desert below Yudujun Mountain, six thousand li northwest of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yinan was overjoyed. He sent envoys bearing local tribute and re-established his royal camp below Yudujun Mountain, north of the great desert, six thousand li northwest of the capital.

sentences.zh: 東至靺鞨，西至葉護，南接沙磧，北至俱倫水，回紇、拔野古、阿跌、同羅、僕骨、霫諸大部落皆屬焉。

translations.literal: East to the Mohe, west to Yehu, south adjoining the sandy desert, north to the Julun River—the great tribes of the Huihe, Bayegu, Adie, Tongluo, Pugu, and Xi all came under his rule.
translations.idiomatic: His domain reached east to the Mohe, west to Yehu, south to the sandy desert, and north to the Julun River. The great tribes of the Huihe, Bayegu, Adie, Tongluo, Pugu, and Xi all submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 三年，夷男遣其弟統特勒來朝，太宗厚加撫接，賜以寶刀及寶鞭。

translations.literal: In the third year, Yinan sent his younger brother Tongtelu to court; Emperor Taizong treated him with great kindness and bestowed a precious knife and a precious whip.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Yinan sent his younger brother Tongtelu to court. Emperor Taizong received him warmly and bestowed a precious knife and whip.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「汝所部有大罪者鞭之。」

translations.literal: He said to him: "For those of your tribe who commit great crimes, whip them."
translations.idiomatic: He told him, "Use this whip on any of your people who commit grave offenses.

sentences.zh: 夷男甚喜。

translations.literal: Yinan was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Yinan was delighted.

sentences.zh: 四年，平突厥頡利之後，朔塞空虛，夷男率其部東返故國，建庭于都尉揵山北，獨邏河之南，在京師北三千三百里；

translations.literal: In the fourth year, after Jieli of the Turks had been pacified, the northern frontier lay empty; Yinan led his tribe east back to their former lands and established his court north of Duyu Jian Mountain, south of the Tuo River alone, three thousand three hundred li north of the capital;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, after Jieli of the Turks had been subdued, the northern frontier stood empty. Yinan led his tribe east back to their former lands and established his court north of Duyu Jian Mountain, on the south bank of the Tuo River alone, three thousand three hundred li north of the capital;

sentences.zh: 東至室韋，西至金山，南至突厥，北臨瀚海，即古匈奴之故地。

translations.literal: East to the Shiwei, west to Jinshan, south to the Turks, north bordering the Hanhai—that is, the former territory of the ancient Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: It reached east to the Shiwei, west to Jinshan, south to the Turks, and north to the Hanhai—the old lands of the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 勝兵二十萬，立其二子爲南北部。

translations.literal: His effective troops numbered two hundred thousand, and he installed his two sons as leaders of the northern and southern divisions.
translations.idiomatic: He could field two hundred thousand fighting men and installed his two sons as heads of the northern and southern divisions.

sentences.zh: 太宗亦以其強盛，恐爲後患。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong also, because of their strength, feared they would become a future trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong also feared that their growing strength might become a future threat.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遣使備禮冊命，拜其二子皆爲小可汗，外示優崇，實欲分其勢也。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he sent envoys with full ceremonial investiture to ennoble both sons as lesser qaghans—outwardly showing favor, but in truth seeking to divide their power.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he sent envoys with full ceremonial investiture to ennoble both sons as lesser qaghans—an outward show of honor, but in truth an attempt to divide their power.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷立李思摩爲可汗，處其部衆于漠南之地。

translations.literal: It happened that the court established Li Simo as qaghan and settled his tribes in the lands south of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: About this time the court established Li Simo as qaghan and settled his tribes south of the desert.

sentences.zh: 夷男心惡思摩，甚不悅。

translations.literal: Yinan hated Simo in his heart and was deeply displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yinan deeply resented Simo and was greatly displeased.

sentences.zh: 十五年，太宗幸洛陽，將有事於太山。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Emperor Taizong visited Luoyang and was about to perform the rites at Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Emperor Taizong went to Luoyang, intending to perform the rites at Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 夷男謀于其國曰：「天子封太山，萬國必會，士馬皆集，邊境空虛，我於此時取思摩如拉朽耳。」

translations.literal: Yinan plotted in his state, saying: "When the Son of Heaven performs the feng at Mount Tai, all states under heaven will assemble, troops and horses will all be gathered, and the frontier will stand empty. If we take Simo at that time, it will be like pulling down rotten wood."
translations.idiomatic: Yinan plotted with his people, saying, "When the Son of Heaven performs the feng rite at Mount Tai, every state will assemble and troops will be drawn away, leaving the frontier empty. If we strike Simo then, it will be like pulling down rotten timber.

sentences.zh: 因命其子大度設勒兵二十萬，屯白道川，據善陽嶺以擊思摩之部。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered his son Dadu She to muster two hundred thousand troops, encamp at Baidao River, and hold Shanyang Ridge to attack Simo's tribe.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore ordered his son Dadu She to muster two hundred thousand troops, encamp along the Baidao River, and seize Shanyang Ridge to attack Simo's tribe.

sentences.zh: 思摩遣使請救，詔英國公李勣、蒲州刺史薛萬徹率步騎數萬赴之。

translations.literal: Simo sent envoys to request rescue; an edict ordered the Duke of Ying, Li Ji, and the prefect of Puzhou, Xue Wanche, to lead several tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: Simo sent envoys begging for aid. An edict ordered the Duke of Ying, Li Ji, and Xue Wanche, prefect of Puzhou, to lead tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 逾白道川至青山，與大度設相及。

translations.literal: They crossed Baidao River to Qingshan and caught up with Dadu She.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed the Baidao River to Qingshan and caught up with Dadu She.

sentences.zh: 追之累月，至諾真水，大度設知不脫，乃互十里而陳兵。

translations.literal: They pursued him for months until they reached Nuozhen River; Dadu She, knowing he could not escape, drew up his troops in battle array at intervals of ten li.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued him for months until they reached the Nuozhen River. Seeing that he could not escape, Dadu She drew up his troops in battle lines ten li apart.

sentences.zh: 先是，延陀擊沙缽羅及阿史那社爾等，以步戰而勝。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Yantuo had attacked Shaboluo and Ashina She'er and others and won by fighting on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Yantuo had defeated Shaboluo, Ashina She'er, and others by fighting on foot.

sentences.zh: 及其將來寇也，先講武于國中，教習步戰；

translations.literal: When they were about to come raiding, they first held military exercises in their state and trained in foot combat;
translations.idiomatic: Before they came to raid, they first held military exercises at home and trained in foot combat;

sentences.zh: 每五人，以一人經習戰陣者使執馬，而四人前戰；

translations.literal: for every five men, one experienced in battle formations was made to hold the horses while four advanced to fight;
translations.idiomatic: for every five men, one veteran of battle held the horses while four advanced to fight;

sentences.zh: 克勝即授馬以追奔，失應接罪至於死，沒其家口，以賞戰人，至是遂行其法。

translations.literal: if victorious they were given horses to pursue the fleeing enemy; failure to support was punished by death, and their households were confiscated to reward the fighters—on this occasion they put that method into practice.
translations.idiomatic: if they won, they were given horses to pursue the fleeing enemy; anyone who failed to support his comrades was put to death and his household confiscated to reward the fighters. On this occasion they put that method into practice.

sentences.zh: 突厥兵先合輒退，延陀乘勝而逐之。

translations.literal: The Turk troops engaged and then withdrew, and the Yantuo pursued them in victory.
translations.idiomatic: The Turk troops engaged and then fell back, and the Yantuo pursued them in victory.

sentences.zh: 勣兵拒擊，而延陀萬矢俱發，傷我戰馬。

translations.literal: Ji's troops resisted the attack, but the Yantuo loosed ten thousand arrows together and wounded our war horses.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's troops met the attack, but the Yantuo loosed volleys of arrows that wounded the Tang war horses.

sentences.zh: 乃令去馬步陣，率長槊數百爲隊，齊奮以沖之，其衆潰散。

translations.literal: He then ordered them to dismount and form an infantry battle line, leading several hundred long-spear units in companies to charge together with full force, and the enemy host broke and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered his men to dismount and form infantry lines, leading companies of several hundred long-spearmen in a mass charge that broke the enemy ranks.

sentences.zh: 副總管薛萬徹率數千騎收其執馬者。

translations.literal: Deputy commander-in-chief Xue Wanche led several thousand cavalry to round up those holding the horses.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commander Xue Wanche led several thousand cavalry to round up the men holding the horses.

sentences.zh: 其衆失馬，莫知所從，因大縱，斬首三千餘級，獲馬萬五千匹，甲仗輜重不可勝計。

translations.literal: Their host, having lost their horses, did not know which way to go; thereupon a great slaughter was made—more than three thousand heads were cut off, fifteen thousand horses were captured, and armor, weapons, and baggage were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Deprived of their horses, the enemy host did not know which way to flee. A great slaughter followed: more than three thousand heads were taken, fifteen thousand horses captured, and armor, weapons, and baggage beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 大度設跳身而遁，萬徹將數百騎追之，弗及。

translations.literal: Dadu She leaped away and fled; Wanche led several hundred cavalry in pursuit but did not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: Dadu She leaped away and fled. Wanche led several hundred cavalry in pursuit but could not catch him.

sentences.zh: 其餘衆大奔走，相騰踐而死者甚衆，伏屍被野。

translations.literal: The rest of the host fled in great disorder; many died trampling one another, and corpses lay strewn across the fields.
translations.idiomatic: The rest of the host fled in disorder. Many were trampled to death, and corpses lay strewn across the plain.

sentences.zh: 夷男因乞與突厥和，並遣使謝罪。

translations.literal: Yinan thereupon begged for peace with the Turks and sent envoys to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Yinan then begged for peace with the Turks and sent envoys to apologize.

sentences.zh: 十六年，遣其叔父沙缽羅泥敦策斤來請婚，獻馬三千匹。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, he sent his uncle Shaboluo Nitun Cejin to request a marriage alliance, presenting three thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he sent his uncle Shaboluo Nitun Cejin to request a marriage alliance, presenting three thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂侍臣曰：「北狄世爲寇亂，今延陀崛強，須早爲之所。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said to his attending ministers: "The northern barbarians have for generations been raiders and rebels; now the Yantuo have risen powerful, and we must deal with them early.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong told his ministers, "The northern peoples have raided and rebelled for generations. Now the Yantuo have grown powerful, and we must deal with them before it is too late.

sentences.zh: 朕熟思之，唯有二策：選徒十萬，擊而虜之，滅除凶醜，百年無事，此一策也；

translations.literal: I have thought it over carefully and see only two plans: select one hundred thousand troops, strike and capture them, wipe out these vicious foes, and have a century of peace—this is one plan;
translations.idiomatic: I have considered the matter carefully and see only two courses: raise one hundred thousand troops, strike and capture them, wipe out these vicious foes, and secure a century of peace—that is one course;

sentences.zh: 若遂其來請，結以婚姻，緩轡羈縻，亦足三十年安靜，此亦一策也。

translations.literal: if we grant their coming request and bind them by marriage, holding the reins loosely to keep them in check, that would also suffice for thirty years of quiet—this too is a plan.
translations.idiomatic: or grant their request and bind them by marriage, holding the reins loosely to keep them in check—that would also buy thirty years of peace. That is the other course.

sentences.zh: 未知何者爲先？」

translations.literal: I do not know which should come first?"
translations.idiomatic: Which should we choose?

sentences.zh: 司空房玄齡對曰：「今大亂之後，瘡痍未復，且兵凶戰危，聖人所慎。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Fang Xuanling replied: "After the great disorders, wounds are not yet healed, and moreover war is inauspicious and perilous—what the sage cautions against.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Fang Xuanling replied, "After the great disorders the realm is still scarred, and war is inauspicious and perilous—what the sage himself warns against.

sentences.zh: 和親之策，實天下幸甚。」

translations.literal: The plan of marriage alliance is truly a great fortune for all under heaven."
translations.idiomatic: A marriage alliance would truly be a blessing for the realm."

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「朕爲蒼生父母，苟可以利之，豈惜一女？」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said: "I am parent to the common people; if a daughter can benefit them, how would I begrudge one?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong said, "I am parent to the common people. If one daughter can benefit them, how could I begrudge her?"

sentences.zh: 遂許以新興公主妻之。

translations.literal: He thereupon promised Princess Xinxing as his wife.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon promised Princess Xinxing in marriage.

sentences.zh: 因征夷男備親迎之禮。

translations.literal: He then summoned Yinan to prepare the ceremonial reception of the bride.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned Yinan to prepare the ceremonial reception of the bride.

sentences.zh: 仍發詔將幸靈州與之會。

translations.literal: He also issued an edict that he would visit Lingzhou to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: He also issued an edict that he would travel to Lingzhou to meet him.

sentences.zh: 夷男大悅，謂其國中曰：「我本鐵勒之小帥也，天子立我爲可汗，今復嫁我公主，車駕親至靈州，斯亦足矣！」

translations.literal: Yinan was greatly pleased and said to his people: "I was originally only a petty chief of the Tiele; the Son of Heaven made me qaghan, and now he gives me a princess in marriage and will come in person to Lingzhou—this is enough!"
translations.idiomatic: Yinan was overjoyed and told his people, "I was only a petty chief of the Tiele. The Son of Heaven made me qaghan, and now he gives me a princess and will come in person to Lingzhou. What more could I ask?

sentences.zh: 於是稅諸部羊馬以爲聘財。

translations.literal: He thereupon levied sheep and horses from the tribes as betrothal gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon levied sheep and horses from the tribes as betrothal gifts.

sentences.zh: 或說夷男曰：「我薛延陀可汗與大唐天子俱一國主，何有自往朝謁？

translations.literal: Someone urged Yinan, saying: "Our Xueyantuo qaghan and the Son of Heaven of Great Tang are both rulers of a state—why should you go in person to pay court?
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged Yinan, "Our Xueyantuo qaghan and the Son of Heaven of Great Tang are both sovereigns of a state. Why should you go in person to pay court?

sentences.zh: 如或拘留，悔之無及！」

translations.literal: If you are detained, it will be too late for regret!"
translations.idiomatic: If you are detained, it will be too late for regret!

sentences.zh: 夷男曰：「吾聞大唐天子聖德遠被，日月所照，皆來賓服。

translations.literal: Yinan said: "I have heard that the Son of Heaven of Great Tang is sage and virtuous, his power reaching far; all that sun and moon shine upon come to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Yinan replied, "I have heard that the Son of Heaven of Great Tang is sage and virtuous, and that all lands touched by sun and moon come to submit.

sentences.zh: 我歸心委質，冀得睹天顏，死無所恨！

translations.literal: I give my heart in loyal submission and hope to behold the imperial countenance—even in death I would have no regret!
translations.idiomatic: I give my heart in loyal submission and hope to behold the imperial countenance. Even in death I would have no regret!

sentences.zh: 然磧北之地，必當有主，舍我別求，固非大國之計。

translations.literal: Yet the lands north of the desert must have a master; to set me aside and seek another would surely not be the great state's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the lands north of the desert must have a master. To set me aside and seek another would not be the great state's plan.

sentences.zh: 我志決矣，勿復多言！」

translations.literal: My mind is made up—say no more!"
translations.idiomatic: My mind is made up. Say no more!"

sentences.zh: 於是言者遂止。

translations.literal: Thereupon those who had spoken fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had urged caution fell silent.

sentences.zh: 太宗乃發使受其羊馬。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong then sent envoys to receive their sheep and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong then sent envoys to receive their sheep and horses.

sentences.zh: 然夷男先無府藏，調斂其國，往返且萬里，既涉沙磧，無水草，羊馬多死，遂後期。

translations.literal: Yet Yinan had had no treasury at first; he levied upon his state, and the round trip was nearly ten thousand li; having crossed the sandy desert where there was no grass or water, many sheep and horses died, and thus they were late.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yinan had no treasury of his own. He levied his whole realm, and the round trip was nearly ten thousand li. Crossing the desert without grass or water, many sheep and horses died, and they arrived late.

sentences.zh: 太宗於是停幸靈州。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong thereupon canceled his visit to Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong thereupon canceled his visit to Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 既而其聘羊馬來至，所耗將半。

translations.literal: When their betrothal sheep and horses finally arrived, nearly half had been lost.
translations.idiomatic: When the betrothal sheep and horses finally arrived, nearly half had been lost on the way.

sentences.zh: 議者以爲夷狄不可禮義畜，若聘財未備而與之婚，或輕中國，當須要其備禮，於是下詔絕其婚。

translations.literal: Critics held that barbarians cannot be kept by ritual and righteousness; if betrothal gifts were not complete yet a marriage were granted, they might slight China—full ceremonial gifts must be required; thereupon an edict broke off the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Critics argued that barbarians cannot be governed by ritual alone; if the betrothal gifts were incomplete yet a marriage were granted, they might slight China. Full ceremonial gifts must be required, and an edict broke off the marriage.

sentences.zh: 既而李思摩數遣兵侵掠之。

translations.literal: Soon after, Li Simo repeatedly sent troops to raid them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Li Simo repeatedly sent troops to raid them.

sentences.zh: 延陀復遣突利失擊思摩，至定襄，抄掠而去。

translations.literal: The Yantuo again sent Tuli Shi to attack Simo, reaching Dingxiang, plundering, and withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: The Yantuo again sent Tuli Shi to attack Simo, reaching Dingxiang, plundering, and withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣英國公李勣援之，見虜已出塞而還。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong sent the Duke of Ying, Li Ji, to their aid; he found the enemy had already left the frontier and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong sent the Duke of Ying, Li Ji, to their aid, but the enemy had already left the frontier and withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 太宗以其數與思摩交兵，璽書責讓之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong, because they had repeatedly fought with Simo, sent an imperial letter rebuking them.
translations.idiomatic: Because they had repeatedly fought with Simo, Emperor Taizong sent an imperial letter rebuking them.

sentences.zh: 十九年，謂其使人曰：「語爾可汗，我父子並東征高麗，汝若能寇邊者，但當來也！」

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, he said to their envoy: "Tell your qaghan: my father and I are both campaigning east against Goguryeo; if you wish to raid the frontier, come whenever you like!"
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he told their envoy, "Tell your qaghan: my father and I are both campaigning east against Goguryeo. If you wish to raid the frontier, come whenever you like!

sentences.zh: 夷男遣使致謝，復請發兵助軍，太宗答以優詔而止。

translations.literal: Yinan sent envoys to express thanks and again requested to send troops to aid the army; Emperor Taizong replied with a gracious edict declining.
translations.idiomatic: Yinan sent envoys to thank him and again offered troops to aid the campaign. Emperor Taizong replied with a gracious edict declining.

sentences.zh: 其冬，太宗拔遼東諸城，破駐蹕陳，而高麗莫離支潛令靺鞨誑惑夷男，啖以厚利，夷男氣懾不敢動。

translations.literal: That winter, Emperor Taizong captured the cities of Liaodong and broke the encampment at Zhubi, while Molichi of Goguryeo secretly had the Mohe deceive Yinan and entice him with rich rewards—Yinan was cowed and did not dare move.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Emperor Taizong captured the cities of Liaodong and broke the encampment at Zhubi. Molichi of Goguryeo secretly had the Mohe deceive Yinan with rich rewards, and Yinan was cowed into inaction.

sentences.zh: 俄而夷男卒，太宗爲之舉哀。

translations.literal: Before long Yinan died, and Emperor Taizong mourned for him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yinan died, and Emperor Taizong mourned for him.

sentences.zh: 夷男少子肆葉護拔灼襲殺其兄突利失可汗而自立，是爲頡利俱利薛沙多彌可汗。

translations.literal: Yinan's youngest son Siyehu Baozhuo attacked and killed his elder brother Qaghan Tuli Shi and installed himself, becoming Qaghan Jieli Julixue Shaduomi.
translations.idiomatic: Yinan's youngest son Siyehu Baozhuo attacked and killed his elder brother Qaghan Tuli Shi and seized power, taking the title Jieli Julixue Shaduomi Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 拔灼性褊急，馭下無恩，多所殺戮，其下不附。

translations.literal: Baozhuo was narrow and impatient by nature, ruled his subordinates without kindness, killed many, and his followers did not attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhuo was narrow-tempered and impatient, ruled without kindness, killed many, and his followers would not stand by him.

sentences.zh: 是時復乙太宗尚在遼東，遂發兵寇夏州，將軍執失思力擊敗之，虜其衆數萬，拔灼輕騎遁去，尋爲回紇所殺，宗族殆盡。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Taizong was still in Liaodong; Baozhuo thereupon raised troops to raid Xiazhou. General Zhishi Sili defeated him and captured several tens of thousands of his followers; Baozhuo fled on light horse and was soon killed by the Huihe, and his clan was nearly wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Taizong was still in Liaodong. Baozhuo thereupon raised troops to raid Xiazhou. General Zhishi Sili defeated him and captured tens of thousands of his followers. Baozhuo fled on a swift horse and was soon killed by the Huihe, and his clan was nearly wiped out.

sentences.zh: 其餘衆尚五六萬，竄於西域，又諸姓俟斤遞相攻擊，各遣使歸命。

translations.literal: The remaining followers, still fifty or sixty thousand, fled into the western regions; moreover the various tribal yabghu attacked one another in turn, each sending envoys to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Some fifty or sixty thousand survivors fled westward. The various tribal leaders attacked one another in turn, each sending envoys to submit.

sentences.zh: 二十年，太宗遣使江夏王道宗、左衛大將軍阿史那社爾爲瀚海道安撫大使；

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, Emperor Taizong sent the Prince of Jiangxia, Li Daozong, and the Grand General of the Left Guard, Ashina She'er, as pacification commissioners of the Hanhai circuit;
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Emperor Taizong sent the Prince of Jiangxia, Li Daozong, and Grand General of the Left Guard Ashina She'er as pacification commissioners of the Hanhai circuit;

sentences.zh: 右領軍大將軍執失思力領突厥兵，代州都督薛萬徹、營州都督張儉、右驍衛大將軍契苾何力各統所部兵分道並進，太宗親幸靈州，爲諸軍聲援。

translations.literal: Grand General of the Right Vanguard Zhishi Sili led Turk troops; the military governor of Daizhou, Xue Wanche, the military governor of Yingzhou, Zhang Jian, and Grand General of the Right Xiaowei Guard Qibi Heli each commanded their own troops advancing by separate routes; Emperor Taizong personally visited Lingzhou to lend support to the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Zhishi Sili led Turk troops; Xue Wanche, military governor of Daizhou, Zhang Jian of Yingzhou, and Grand General Qibi Heli each led their forces by separate routes. Emperor Taizong went in person to Lingzhou to support the armies.

sentences.zh: 既而道宗渡磧，遇延陀余衆數萬來拒戰。

translations.literal: Soon after, Daozong crossed the desert and encountered several tens of thousands of remaining Yantuo coming to resist in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong crossed the desert and encountered tens of thousands of remaining Yantuo who came to resist.

sentences.zh: 道宗擊破之，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: Daozong defeated them and cut off more than a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong defeated them and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 萬徹又與回紇相遇，二將各遣使諭以綏懷之意。

translations.literal: Wanche also met the Huihe; the two generals each sent envoys to explain their intent to pacify and comfort.
translations.idiomatic: Wanche also met the Huihe. Both generals sent envoys to explain their intent to pacify and reassure them.

sentences.zh: 其酋帥見使者，皆頓顙歡呼，請入朝。

translations.literal: Their chieftains, seeing the envoys, all bowed their foreheads to the ground and shouted for joy, requesting to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: Their chieftains, seeing the envoys, all bowed their foreheads to the ground and shouted for joy, asking to come to court.

sentences.zh: 太宗至靈州，其鐵勒諸部相繼至數千人，仍請列爲州縣，北荒悉平。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong reached Lingzhou, the Tiele tribes came in succession by the thousands and still requested to be organized as prefectures and counties; the northern wilds were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong reached Lingzhou, Tiele tribes arrived in succession by the thousands and asked to be organized as prefectures and counties. The northern frontier was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：

translations.literal: An edict said:
translations.idiomatic: An edict proclaimed:

sentences.zh: 惟天爲大，合其德者弗違；

translations.literal: Only Heaven is great; none who unite with its virtue can defy it;
translations.idiomatic: Only Heaven is great; none who unite with its virtue can defy it;

sentences.zh: 謂地蓋厚，體其仁者光被。

translations.literal: we say the earth is thick; those who embody its benevolence shine forth.
translations.idiomatic: the earth is vast, and those who embody its benevolence shine across the world.

sentences.zh: 故能彌倫八極，輿蓋二儀，振絕代之英聲，畢天下之能事。

translations.literal: Thus one can span the eight extremities, bear up heaven and earth, raise a peerless heroic renown, and accomplish all that is possible under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one may span the eight directions, bear up heaven and earth, raise a peerless heroic renown, and accomplish all that is possible under heaven.

sentences.zh: 彼匈奴者，與開闢而俱生；

translations.literal: Those Xiongnu arose together with the opening of the world;
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu arose together with the opening of the world;

sentences.zh: 奄有龍庭，共上皇而並列。

translations.literal: they held the Dragon Court and stood as peers to the Supreme Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: they held the Dragon Court and stood as peers to the Supreme Emperor.

sentences.zh: 僭稱驕子，分天街於紫宸；

translations.literal: They arrogantly styled themselves favored sons and divided the Heavenly Street at Zichen;
translations.idiomatic: They arrogantly styled themselves favored sons and divided the Heavenly Street at Zichen;

sentences.zh: 仰應旄頭，抗大禮於皇極。

translations.literal: they looked up to answer the Bushel Star and resisted the great rites at the imperial pole.
translations.idiomatic: they looked up to answer the Bushel Star and resisted the great rites at the imperial pole.

sentences.zh: 糸面窺邃古，能無力制。

translations.literal: Gazing back into remote antiquity, who could restrain them by force?
translations.idiomatic: Gazing back into remote antiquity, who could restrain them by force alone?

sentences.zh: 自朕臨御天下，二紀於茲，粵以眇身，一匡寰宇。

translations.literal: Since I ascended to rule all under heaven, two reign-periods have passed; with this slight person I have set the realm aright.
translations.idiomatic: Since I ascended to rule all under heaven, two reign-periods have passed; with my own slight person I have set the realm aright.

sentences.zh: 始勤勞於昧旦，終致治於升平。

translations.literal: At first I toiled from dawn; in the end I brought the realm to rising peace.
translations.idiomatic: At first I toiled from dawn; in the end I brought the realm to lasting peace.

sentences.zh: 曩者聊命偏師，遂擒頡利；

translations.literal: Earlier I merely ordered a detached force and thus captured Jieli;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier I merely ordered a detached force and captured Jieli;

sentences.zh: 今茲始弘廟略，已滅延陀。

translations.literal: now for the first time I have expanded the imperial plan and already destroyed the Yantuo.
translations.idiomatic: now I have expanded the imperial plan and destroyed the Yantuo.

sentences.zh: 雖麾駕出征，未逾郊甸；

translations.literal: Although the imperial carriage went forth on campaign, it did not pass beyond the suburban districts;
translations.idiomatic: Although the imperial carriage went forth on campaign, it did not pass beyond the suburban districts;

sentences.zh: 前驅所轥，才掩塞垣。

translations.literal: what the vanguard overran barely covered the frontier ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: what the vanguard overran barely covered the frontier ramparts.

sentences.zh: 長策風行，已振金徽之表，揚威電發，遠璟沙場之外。

translations.literal: Long plans moved like the wind and already shook the lands beyond the golden frontier; glory flashed like lightning and reached far beyond the desert battlefield.
translations.idiomatic: Long plans moved like the wind and shook the lands beyond the frontier; glory flashed like lightning and reached far beyond the desert battlefield.

sentences.zh: 鐵勒諸姓、回紇胡祿俟利發等，總百余萬戶，散處北溟，遠遣使人，委身內屬，請同編列，並爲州郡。

translations.literal: The Tiele clans, the Huihe, the Hulü Toli, and others—in all more than a million households scattered in the northern sea—sent envoys from afar to submit in person, requesting to be enrolled together and made into prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiele clans, the Huihe, the Hulü Toli, and others—more than a million households scattered across the northern sea—sent envoys from afar to submit in person, asking to be enrolled as prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 收其瀚海，盡入提封；

translations.literal: Their Hanhai was taken in and fully entered the imperial domain;
translations.idiomatic: Their Hanhai was taken in and fully entered the imperial domain;

sentences.zh: 解其辮發，並垂冠帶。

translations.literal: their braided hair was undone and they all wore caps and belts.
translations.idiomatic: their braided hair was undone and they all wore caps and belts.

sentences.zh: 上變星昴，歸於東井之躔；

translations.literal: Above, the stars of the Bushel changed and returned to the mansion of the Well;
translations.idiomatic: Above, the stars of the Bushel changed and returned to the mansion of the Well;

sentences.zh: 下掩蹛林，袪入南山之囿。

translations.literal: below, the steppe forests were covered and drawn into the southern mountain parks.
translations.idiomatic: below, the steppe forests were covered and drawn into the southern mountain parks.

sentences.zh: 混元已降，殊未前聞；

translations.literal: Since the primordial unity descended, nothing like this has been heard before;
translations.idiomatic: Since the primordial unity descended, nothing like this has been heard before;

sentences.zh: 無疆之業，永貽來裔。

translations.literal: this boundless achievement will be handed down to posterity forever.
translations.idiomatic: this boundless achievement will be handed down to posterity forever.

sentences.zh: 古人所不能致，今既吞之；

translations.literal: What the ancients could not attain, we have now swallowed up;
translations.idiomatic: What the ancients could not attain, we have now swallowed up;

sentences.zh: 前王所不能屈，今鹹滅之。

translations.literal: what former kings could not subdue, we have now all extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: what former kings could not subdue, we have now all extinguished.

sentences.zh: 斯實書契所未有，古今之壯觀，豈朕一人獨能宣力！

translations.literal: This is truly what the written records have never had—a spectacle of past and present. How could I alone have proclaimed such power!
translations.idiomatic: This is truly what the written records have never recorded—a spectacle of past and present. How could I alone have accomplished such power!

sentences.zh: 蓋由上靈儲祉，錫乙太康；

translations.literal: It is because the Supreme Spirit stored blessings and bestowed great peace;
translations.idiomatic: It is because the Supreme Spirit stored blessings and bestowed great peace;

sentences.zh: 宗廟威靈，成茲克定。

translations.literal: the awe of the ancestral temples accomplished this conquest.
translations.idiomatic: the awe of the ancestral temples accomplished this conquest.

sentences.zh: 即宜備禮，告於清廟，仍頒示普天。

translations.literal: At once full rites should be prepared to report to the Pure Temple, and it should also be proclaimed throughout all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: At once full rites should be prepared to report to the Pure Temple, and it should also be proclaimed throughout all under heaven.

sentences.zh: 其後延陀西遁之衆，共推夷男兄子咄摩支爲伊特勿失可汗，率部落七萬餘口，西歸故地。

translations.literal: Afterward the Yantuo who had fled west jointly enthroned Yinan's elder brother's son Duomozhi as Yite Wushi Qaghan, leading a tribe of more than seventy thousand persons back west to their former lands.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the Yantuo who had fled west jointly enthroned Yinan's nephew Duomozhi as Yite Wushi Qaghan and led more than seventy thousand people back west to their former lands.

sentences.zh: 乃去可汗之號，遣使奉表，請居郁督軍山北。

translations.literal: He then relinquished the title of qaghan, sent envoys with a memorial, and requested to dwell north of Yudujun Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He relinquished the title of qaghan, sent envoys with a memorial, and asked to dwell north of Yudujun Mountain.

sentences.zh: 詔兵部尚書崔敦禮就加綏撫。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Minister of War, Cui Dunli, to go and add further pacification.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Minister of War Cui Dunli to go and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 而諸部鐵勒素服薛延陀之衆，及咄摩支至，九姓渠帥莫不危懼。

translations.literal: The Tiele tribes had long submitted to the Xueyantuo host; when Duomozhi arrived, none of the nine-clan chieftains was not filled with dread.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiele tribes had long submitted to the Xueyantuo. When Duomozhi arrived, every chieftain of the nine clans was filled with dread.

sentences.zh: 朝議恐爲磧北之患，復令英國公李勣進加討擊。

translations.literal: The court feared he would become a trouble north of the desert and again ordered the Duke of Ying, Li Ji, to advance and attack.
translations.idiomatic: The court feared he would become a threat north of the desert and again ordered the Duke of Ying, Li Ji, to attack.

sentences.zh: 勣率九姓鐵勒二萬騎至於天山。

translations.literal: Ji led twenty thousand cavalry of the nine-clan Tiele to Tianshan.
translations.idiomatic: Ji led twenty thousand cavalry of the nine-clan Tiele to Tianshan.

sentences.zh: 咄摩支見官軍奄至，惶駭不知所爲；

translations.literal: Duomozhi, seeing the government troops suddenly arrive, was terrified and did not know what to do;
translations.idiomatic: Duomozhi, seeing government troops suddenly arrive, was terrified and did not know what to do;

sentences.zh: 且聞詔使蕭嗣業在回紇中，因而請降。

translations.literal: moreover he heard that the imperial envoy Xiao Siye was among the Huihe, and therefore requested to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: he also heard that the imperial envoy Xiao Siye was among the Huihe, and therefore requested to surrender.

sentences.zh: 嗣業與之俱至京師，詔授右武衛將軍，賜以田宅。

translations.literal: Siye came with him to the capital; an edict appointed him General of the Right Martial Guard and bestowed fields and a residence.
translations.idiomatic: Siye came with him to the capital. An edict appointed Duomozhi General of the Right Martial Guard and bestowed fields and a residence.

sentences.zh: 咄摩支入國後，鐵勒酋帥潛知其部落，仍持兩端。

translations.literal: After Duomozhi entered the realm, Tiele chieftains secretly knew of his tribe and still kept to both sides.
translations.idiomatic: After Duomozhi entered the realm, Tiele chieftains still knew where his tribe was and kept their options open.

sentences.zh: 李勣因縱兵追擊，前後斬五千餘級，虜男女三萬計。

translations.literal: Li Ji thereupon unleashed his troops in pursuit; in all more than five thousand heads were cut off and some thirty thousand men and women were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji unleashed his troops in pursuit, cutting off more than five thousand heads and capturing some thirty thousand men and women.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，契苾、回紇等十余部落以薛延陀亡散殆盡，乃相繼歸國。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, more than ten tribes including the Qibi and Huihe, because the Xueyantuo had perished and scattered almost entirely, returned to the realm in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, more than ten tribes including the Qibi and Huihe, with the Xueyantuo nearly destroyed and scattered, returned to the realm in succession.

sentences.zh: 太宗各因其地土，擇其部落，置爲州府：以回紇部爲瀚海都督府，僕骨爲金徽都督府，多覽葛爲燕然都督府，拔野古部爲幽陵都督府，同羅部爲龜林都督府，思結部爲盧山都督府，渾部爲皋蘭州，斛薛部爲高闕州，奚結部爲雞鹿州，阿跌部爲雞田州，契苾部爲榆溪州，思結別部爲蹛林州，白霫部爲寘顏州，凡一十三州。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong, according to each group's territory, selected their tribes and established them as prefectures and protectorates: the Huihe as Hanhai Protectorate, the Pugu as Jinwei Protectorate, the Duolange as Yanran Protectorate, the Bayegu as Youling Protectorate, the Tongluo as Guilin Protectorate, the Sijie as Lushan Protectorate, the Hun as Gaolan Prefecture, the Huxue as Gaoque Prefecture, the Xijie as Jilu Prefecture, the Adie as Jitian Prefecture, the Qibi as Yuxi Prefecture, a separate branch of the Sijie as Dianlin Prefecture, the Baixi as Zhiyan Prefecture—in all thirteen prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong established thirteen prefectures and protectorates according to each tribe's territory: the Huihe as Hanhai Protectorate, the Pugu as Jinwei, the Duolange as Yanran, the Bayegu as Youling, the Tongluo as Guilin, the Sijie as Lushan, the Hun as Gaolan, the Huxue as Gaoque, the Xijie as Jilu, the Adie as Jitian, the Qibi as Yuxi, a Sijie branch as Dianlin, and the Baixi as Zhiyan.

sentences.zh: 拜其酋長爲都督、刺史，給玄金魚以爲符信，又置燕然都護以統之。

translations.literal: Their chieftains were appointed protectors and prefects, given black-gold fish tally tokens as credentials, and a Yanran Protector-General was also established to govern them.
translations.idiomatic: Their chieftains were appointed protectors and prefects, given black-gold fish tally tokens as credentials, and a Yanran Protector-General was established to govern them.

sentences.zh: 是歲，太宗以鐵勒諸部並皆內屬，詔賜京城百姓大酺三日。

translations.literal: That year, because all the Tiele tribes had submitted, Emperor Taizong ordered a great feast of three days for the people of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That year, because all the Tiele tribes had submitted, Emperor Taizong ordered a three-day feast for the people of the capital.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年，延陀首領先逃逸者請歸國，高宗更置溪彈州以安恤之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghui, Yantuo chieftains who had fled earlier requested to return; Emperor Gaozong re-established Xidan Prefecture to pacify and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yonghui, Yantuo chieftains who had fled earlier asked to return. Emperor Gaozong re-established Xidan Prefecture to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 至則天時，突厥強盛，鐵勒諸部在漠北者漸爲所並。

translations.literal: By the time of Empress Wu, the Turks were powerful, and the Tiele tribes north of the desert were gradually absorbed by them.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of Empress Wu the Turks were powerful, and the Tiele tribes north of the desert were gradually absorbed by them.

sentences.zh: 回紇、契苾、思結、渾部徙于甘、涼二州之地。

translations.literal: The Huihe, Qibi, Sijie, and Hun tribes were moved to the territory of Gan and Liang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The Huihe, Qibi, Sijie, and Hun tribes were moved to the territory of Gan and Liang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 其骨利幹北距大海，去京師最遠，自古未通中國。

translations.literal: The Guligan bordered the great sea to the north, were farthest from the capital, and from antiquity had had no contact with China.
translations.idiomatic: The Guligan bordered the great sea to the north, were farthest from the capital, and from antiquity had had no contact with China.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中遣使來朝貢，遣雲麾將軍康蘇密往慰撫之，仍列其地爲玄闕州。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era they sent envoys to court with tribute; the Cloud Banner General Kang Sumi was sent to comfort and pacify them, and their territory was listed as Xuanque Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era they sent envoys to court with tribute. Cloud Banner General Kang Sumi was sent to comfort them, and their territory was listed as Xuanque Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 俄又遣使隨蘇密使入朝，獻良馬十匹。

translations.literal: Soon after they again sent envoys following Sumi's mission to court, presenting ten fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after they sent envoys following Sumi's mission to court, presenting ten fine horses.

sentences.zh: 太宗奇其駿異，爲之制名。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong marveled at their exceptional swiftness and gave them names.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong marveled at their exceptional swiftness and gave them names.

sentences.zh: 號爲十驥：一曰騰霜白，二曰皎雪驄，三曰凝露驄，四曰懸光驄，五曰決波騟，六曰飛霞驃，七曰發電赤，八曰流金𩢍，九曰翱麟紫，十曰奔虹赤。

translations.literal: They were named the Ten Steeds: first Tengshuangbai, second Jiaoxuecong, third Ninglucong, fourth Xuanguangcong, fifth Jueboju, sixth Feixiapiao, seventh Fadianchi, eighth Liujinju, ninth Aolinzi, tenth Benhongchi.
translations.idiomatic: They were named the Ten Steeds: Tengshuangbai, Jiaoxuecong, Ninglucong, Xuanguangcong, Jueboju, Feixiapiao, Fadianchi, Liujinju, Aolinzi, and Benhongchi.

sentences.zh: 又爲文以敘其事。

translations.literal: He also composed a text to narrate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He also composed a text to narrate the matter.

sentences.zh: 自延陀叛後，朝貢遂絕。

translations.literal: After the Yantuo rebellion, tribute to court ceased.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yantuo rebellion, tribute to court ceased.

sentences.zh: 契丹，居潢水之南，黃龍之北，鮮卑之故地，在京城東北五千三百里。

translations.literal: The Khitan dwelt south of the Huangshui and north of the Yellow Dragon—the former land of the Xianbei, five thousand three hundred li northeast of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan dwelt south of the Huangshui and north of the Yellow Dragon—the former land of the Xianbei, five thousand three hundred li northeast of the capital.

sentences.zh: 東與高麗鄰，西與奚國接，南至營州，北至室韋。

translations.literal: East they bordered Goguryeo, west they met the Xi state, south to Yingzhou, north to the Shiwei.
translations.idiomatic: To the east they bordered Goguryeo, to the west the Xi, to the south Yingzhou, and to the north the Shiwei.

sentences.zh: 冷陘山在其國南，與奚西山相崎，地方二千里。

translations.literal: Lengling Mountain was in the south of their state, facing the western mountains of the Xi; their territory was two thousand li square.
translations.idiomatic: Lengling Mountain lay in the south of their state, facing the western mountains of the Xi. Their territory was two thousand li square.

sentences.zh: 逐獵往來，居無常處。

translations.literal: They moved about in pursuit of the hunt and had no fixed dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: They moved about in pursuit of the hunt and had no fixed dwelling.

sentences.zh: 其君長姓大賀氏。

translations.literal: Their chieftains bore the surname Dahe.
translations.idiomatic: Their chieftains bore the surname Dahe.

sentences.zh: 勝兵四萬三千人，分爲八部，若有徵發，諸部皆須議合。

translations.literal: Their effective troops numbered forty-three thousand, divided into eight tribes; if there was a mobilization, all tribes had to deliberate together.
translations.idiomatic: They could field forty-three thousand fighting men, divided into eight tribes. Any mobilization required all tribes to deliberate together.

sentences.zh: 不得獨舉。

translations.literal: None could act alone.
translations.idiomatic: None could act alone.

sentences.zh: 獵則別部，戰則同行。

translations.literal: In hunting they went by separate tribes; in war they marched together.
translations.idiomatic: In hunting they went by separate tribes; in war they marched together.

sentences.zh: 本臣突厥，好與奚鬥，不利則遁保青山及鮮卑山。

translations.literal: They had long submitted to the Turks, loved to fight the Xi, and when at a disadvantage fled to hold Qing Mountain and Xianbei Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: They had long submitted to the Turks, loved to fight the Xi, and when at a disadvantage fled to Qing Mountain and Xianbei Mountain.

sentences.zh: 其俗死者不得作冢墓，以馬駕車送入大山，置之樹上，亦無服紀。

translations.literal: By custom the dead might not be given tombs; they were taken by horse-drawn cart into the great mountains and placed in trees, and there was no mourning dress or observance.
translations.idiomatic: By custom the dead were not given tombs. They were taken by horse-drawn cart into the mountains and placed in trees, and there was no mourning dress or observance.

sentences.zh: 子孫死，父母晨夕哭之；

translations.literal: when children died, parents wept morning and evening;
translations.idiomatic: When children died, parents wept morning and evening;

sentences.zh: 父母死，子孫不哭。

translations.literal: when parents died, children did not weep.
translations.idiomatic: when parents died, children did not weep.

sentences.zh: 其餘風俗與突厥同。

translations.literal: Their other customs were the same as those of the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Their other customs were the same as those of the Turks.

sentences.zh: 武德初，數抄邊境。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude they repeatedly raided the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wude era they repeatedly raided the frontier.

sentences.zh: 二年，入寇平州。

translations.literal: In the second year they invaded Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year they invaded Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年，其君長咄羅遣使貢名馬豐貂。

translations.literal: In the sixth year their chieftain Zhuoluo sent envoys presenting famous horses and rich sable furs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year their chieftain Zhuoluo sent envoys presenting famous horses and rich sable furs.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年，其君摩會率其部落來降。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan their chief Mohui led his tribe to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenguan their chief Mohui led his tribe to submit.

sentences.zh: 突厥頡利遣使請以梁師都易契丹，太宗謂曰：「契丹、突厥，本是別類，今來降我，何故索之？

translations.literal: Jieli of the Turks sent envoys requesting to exchange Liang Shidu for the Khitan; Emperor Taizong said: "The Khitan and Turks are originally separate kinds; now they have come to submit to me—why should you demand them?
translations.idiomatic: Jieli of the Turks sent envoys asking to exchange Liang Shidu for the Khitan. Emperor Taizong said, "The Khitan and Turks are separate peoples. They have come to submit to me—why should I give them up?

sentences.zh: 師都本中國人，據我州城，以爲盜竊，突厥無故容納之，我師往討，便來救援。

translations.literal: Shidu is originally a man of China who seized our prefectural cities as a bandit; the Turks harbored him without cause, and when our army went to punish him, you came to his rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Shidu is a Chinese subject who seized our cities as a bandit. The Turks harbored him without cause, and when our army went to punish him, you came to his rescue.

sentences.zh: 計不久自當擒滅。

translations.literal: I reckon he will soon be captured and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: I reckon he will soon be captured and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 縱其不得，終不以契丹易之。」

translations.literal: Even if he is not taken, I would never exchange the Khitan for him."
translations.idiomatic: Even if he is not taken, I would never exchange the Khitan for him."

sentences.zh: 太宗伐高麗，至營州，會其君長及老人等，賜物各有差，授其蕃長窟哥爲左武衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong campaigned against Goguryeo and reached Yingzhou, he met their chieftains and elders, bestowed gifts in varying measure, and appointed their tribal chief Kuge as General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong campaigned against Goguryeo and reached Yingzhou, he met their chieftains and elders, bestowed gifts in varying measure, and appointed their tribal chief Kuge as General of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，窟哥等部咸請內屬，乃置松漠都督府，以窟哥爲左領軍將軍兼松漠都督府、無極縣男，賜姓李氏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, Kuge's tribe and others all requested to submit; the Songmo Protectorate was established, and Kuge was made General of the Left Vanguard Army and concurrently Protector of Songmo and Baron of Wuji County, granted the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Kuge's tribe and others all asked to submit. The Songmo Protectorate was established, and Kuge was made General of the Left Vanguard Army and Protector of Songmo, Baron of Wuji County, with the surname Li.

sentences.zh: 顯慶初，又拜窟哥爲左監門大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianqing, Kuge was again appointed Grand General of the Left Gate Guards.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xianqing, Kuge was again appointed Grand General of the Left Gate Guards.

sentences.zh: 其曾孫祜莫離，則天時曆左衛將軍兼檢校彈汗州刺史，歸順郡王。

translations.literal: His great-grandson Humoli, in the time of Empress Wu, served as General of the Left Guard and concurrently acting prefect of Tanhan, Prince of Guishun Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Humoli, in the time of Empress Wu, served as General of the Left Guard and acting prefect of Tanhan, Prince of Guishun Commandery.

sentences.zh: 又契丹有別部酋帥孫敖曹，初仕隋爲金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: There was also a separate Khitan chieftain, Sun Aocao, who had first served the Sui as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a separate Khitan chieftain, Sun Aocao, who had first served the Sui as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 武德四年，與靺鞨酋長突地稽俱遣使內附，詔令于營州城傍安置，授雲麾將軍，行遼州總管。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, together with the Mohe chieftain Tudi Ji, he sent envoys to submit; an edict ordered them settled beside Yingzhou city, and he was appointed Cloud Banner General and acting military governor of Liaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Wude, together with the Mohe chieftain Tudi Ji, he sent envoys to submit. An edict ordered them settled beside Yingzhou city, and he was appointed Cloud Banner General and acting military governor of Liaozhou.

sentences.zh: 至曾孫萬榮，垂拱初累授右玉鈐衛將軍、歸誠州刺史，封永樂縣公。

translations.literal: Down to his great-grandson Wanrong, at the beginning of Chuigong he was repeatedly appointed General of the Right Jade Bell Guard and prefect of Guicheng, enfeoffed as Duke of Yongle County.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Wanrong, at the beginning of Chuigong, was repeatedly appointed General of the Right Jade Bell Guard and prefect of Guicheng, enfeoffed as Duke of Yongle County.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天中，萬榮與其妹婿松漠都督李盡忠，俱爲營州都督趙翽所侵侮，二人遂舉兵殺翽，據營州作亂。

translations.literal: In the Wansui Tongtian era, Wanrong and his brother-in-law, Protector of Songmo Li Jinzhong, were both insulted by the military governor of Yingzhou, Zhao Hui; the two thereupon raised troops, killed Hui, seized Yingzhou, and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wansui Tongtian era, Wanrong and his brother-in-law, Protector of Songmo Li Jinzhong, were both insulted by the military governor of Yingzhou, Zhao Hui. The two raised troops, killed Hui, seized Yingzhou, and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 盡忠即窟哥之胤，歷位右武衛大將軍兼松漠都督。

translations.literal: Jinzhong was a descendant of Kuge and had held the posts of Grand General of the Right Martial Guard and concurrently Protector of Songmo.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong was a descendant of Kuge and had held the posts of Grand General of the Right Martial Guard and Protector of Songmo.

sentences.zh: 則天怒其叛亂，下詔改萬榮名爲萬斬，盡忠爲盡滅。

translations.literal: Empress Wu, enraged at their rebellion, issued an edict changing Wanrong's name to Wanzhan and Jinzhong's to Jinmie.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu, enraged at their rebellion, issued an edict changing Wanrong's name to Wanzhan and Jinzhong's to Jinmie.

sentences.zh: 盡滅尋自稱無上可汗，以萬斬爲大將，前鋒略地，所向皆下，旬日兵至數萬，進逼檀州。

translations.literal: Jinmie soon styled himself Supreme Qaghan, made Wanzhan his great general, and with the vanguard seized territory—wherever they went, all submitted; within ten days their troops reached tens of thousands and advanced to threaten Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jinmie soon styled himself Supreme Qaghan and made Wanzhan his great general. The vanguard seized territory wherever it went; within ten days their troops reached tens of thousands and advanced on Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔令右金吾大將軍張玄遇、左鷹揚衛將軍曹仁師、司農少卿麻仁節率兵討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Grand General of the Right Golden Crow, Zhang Xianyu, the General of the Left Eagle-Flying Guard, Cao Renshi, and the Vice Minister of Agriculture Ma Renjie to lead troops against them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Grand General Zhang Xianyu of the Right Golden Crow, General Cao Renshi of the Left Eagle-Flying Guard, and Vice Minister of Agriculture Ma Renjie to lead troops against them.

sentences.zh: 與萬斬戰于西硤石穀，官軍敗績，玄遇、仁節並爲賊所虜。

translations.literal: They fought Wanzhan at West Xiashi Valley; the government army was defeated, and Xianyu and Renjie were both captured by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: They fought Wanzhan at West Xiashi Valley. The government army was defeated, and Xianyu and Renjie were both captured.

sentences.zh: 又令夏官尚書王孝傑、左羽林將軍蘇宏暉領兵七萬以繼之。

translations.literal: Wang Xiaojie, Minister of Summer Affairs, and Su Honghui, General of the Left Forest of Feathers, were again ordered to lead seventy thousand troops to follow up.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiaojie, Minister of Summer Affairs, and Su Honghui, General of the Left Forest of Feathers, were ordered to lead seventy thousand troops to follow up.

sentences.zh: 與萬斬戰于東硤石穀，孝傑在陣陷沒。

translations.literal: They fought Wanzhan at East Xiashi Valley; Xiaojie fell in battle.
translations.idiomatic: They fought Wanzhan at East Xiashi Valley, and Xiaojie fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 宏暉棄甲而遁。

translations.literal: Honghui cast off his armor and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Honghui cast off his armor and fled.

sentences.zh: 萬斬乘勝度其衆入幽州，殺略人吏。

translations.literal: Wanzhan, riding his victory, led his host across into Youzhou and killed and plundered officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: Wanzhan, riding his victory, led his host into Youzhou and killed and plundered officials and people.

sentences.zh: 清邊道大總管、建安郡王武攸宜遣裨將討之，不能克。

translations.literal: Wu Youyi, Prince of Jian'an and commander-in-chief of the Qingbian circuit, sent subordinate generals against them but could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Youyi, Prince of Jian'an and commander-in-chief of the Qingbian circuit, sent subordinate generals against them but could not overcome them.

sentences.zh: 又詔左金吾大將軍、河內王武懿宗爲大總管，御史大夫婁師德爲副大總管，右武衛將軍沙吒忠義爲前軍總管，率兵三十萬以討之。

translations.literal: An edict again appointed Wu Yizong, Prince of Henei and Grand General of the Left Golden Crow, as commander-in-chief, the Censor-in-Chief Lou Shide as deputy commander-in-chief, and Shazha Zhongyi, General of the Right Martial Guard, as vanguard commander, to lead three hundred thousand troops against them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Wu Yizong, Prince of Henei and Grand General of the Left Golden Crow, as commander-in-chief, Censor-in-Chief Lou Shide as deputy, and Shazha Zhongyi, General of the Right Martial Guard, as vanguard commander, to lead three hundred thousand troops against them.

sentences.zh: 俄而李盡滅死，萬斬代領其衆。

translations.literal: Before long Li Jinmie died, and Wanzhan took command of his host in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Jinmie died, and Wanzhan took command of his host.

sentences.zh: 萬斬又遣別帥駱務整、何阿小爲游軍前鋒，攻陷冀州，殺刺史陸寶積，屠官吏子女數千人。

translations.literal: Wanzhan again sent the separate commanders Luo Wuzheng and He Axiao as mobile vanguard, captured Jizhou, killed the prefect Lu Baoji, and slaughtered several thousand officials, clerks, and their children.
translations.idiomatic: Wanzhan sent separate commanders Luo Wuzheng and He Axiao as mobile vanguard. They captured Jizhou, killed Prefect Lu Baoji, and slaughtered several thousand officials and their families.

sentences.zh: 俄而奚及突厥之衆掩擊其後，掠其幼弱。

translations.literal: Before long the Xi and Turks struck them from behind and carried off their women and children.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Xi and Turks struck from behind and carried off their women and children.

sentences.zh: 萬斬棄其衆，以輕騎數千人東走。

translations.literal: Wanzhan abandoned his host and fled east with several thousand light cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Wanzhan abandoned his host and fled east with several thousand light cavalry.

sentences.zh: 前軍副總管張九節率數百騎設伏以邀之。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiujie, deputy commander of the vanguard, led several hundred cavalry in ambush to intercept him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiujie, deputy vanguard commander, led several hundred cavalry in ambush to intercept him.

sentences.zh: 萬斬窮蹙，乃將其家奴輕騎宵遁，至潞河東，解鞍憩于林下，其奴斬之。

translations.literal: Wanzhan, hard pressed, took his household slaves and fled by night on light horse; east of the Lu River he dismounted to rest under the trees, and his slave beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, Wanzhan fled by night with his household slaves on light horses. East of the Lu River he dismounted to rest under the trees, and a slave beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 張九節傳其首於東都，自是其餘衆遂降突厥。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiujie sent his head to the eastern capital; from then on the rest of his host submitted to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiujie sent his head to the eastern capital. From then on the rest of his host submitted to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 開元三年，其首領李失活以默啜政衰，率種落內附。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaiyuan, their chieftain Li Shihuo, because Mojie's rule had declined, led his tribe to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaiyuan their chieftain Li Shihuo, seeing Mojie's power wane, led his tribe to submit.

sentences.zh: 失活，即盡忠之從父弟也。

translations.literal: Shihuo was Jinzhong's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Shihuo was Jinzhong's younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 於是復置松漠都督府。

translations.literal: The Songmo Protectorate was thereupon re-established.
translations.idiomatic: The Songmo Protectorate was thereupon re-established.

sentences.zh: 封失活爲松漠郡王，拜左金吾衛大將軍兼松漠都督。

translations.literal: Shihuo was enfeoffed as Prince of Songmo Commandery and appointed Grand General of the Left Golden Crow Guard and concurrently Protector of Songmo.
translations.idiomatic: Shihuo was enfeoffed as Prince of Songmo Commandery and appointed Grand General of the Left Golden Crow Guard and Protector of Songmo.

sentences.zh: 其所統八部落，各因舊帥拜爲刺史，又以將軍薛泰督軍以鎮撫之。

translations.literal: The eight tribes under his command each had their former chiefs appointed prefects, and General Xue Tai was also sent to command troops to pacify and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: The eight tribes under his command each had their former chiefs appointed prefects, and General Xue Tai was sent to command troops to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 明年，失活入朝，封宗室外甥女楊氏爲永樂公主以妻之。

translations.literal: The next year Shihuo came to court; a clanswoman of the imperial house, the Lady Yang, was enfeoffed as Princess Yongle and given to him in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Shihuo came to court. A clanswoman of the imperial house, Lady Yang, was enfeoffed as Princess Yongle and given to him in marriage.

sentences.zh: 六年，失活死，上爲之舉哀，贈特進。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Shihuo died; the emperor mourned for him and posthumously granted the title of Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Shihuo died. The emperor mourned for him and posthumously granted the title of Special Advancement.

sentences.zh: 失活從父弟娑固代統其衆，遣使冊立，仍令襲其兄官爵。

translations.literal: Shihuo's younger cousin Suogu succeeded to command of his host; envoys were sent to invest him, and he was still ordered to inherit his elder brother's offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: Shihuo's younger cousin Suogu succeeded to command of his people. Envoys were sent to invest him, and he was ordered to inherit his elder brother's offices and titles.

sentences.zh: 娑固大臣可突于驍勇，頗得衆心，娑固謀欲除之。

translations.literal: Suogu's minister Ketuyu was fierce and valiant, and greatly won the hearts of the people; Suogu plotted to eliminate him.
translations.idiomatic: Suogu's minister Ketuyu was fierce and valiant and had won strong popular support, so Suogu plotted to eliminate him.

sentences.zh: 可突於反攻娑固，娑固奔營州。

translations.literal: Ketuyu counterattacked Suogu, and Suogu fled to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ketuyu counterattacked Suogu, and Suogu fled to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 都督許欽淡令薛泰帥驍勇五百人，又征奚王李大輔者及娑固合衆以討可突於。

translations.literal: Protector Xu Qindan ordered Xue Tai to lead five hundred elite warriors, and also summoned Xi King Li Dafu and Suogu to combine their hosts to attack Ketuyu.
translations.idiomatic: Protector Xu Qindan ordered Xue Tai to lead five hundred elite troops and also summoned the Xi king Li Dafu and Suogu to combine forces and attack Ketuyu.

sentences.zh: 官軍不利，娑固、大輔臨陣皆爲可突於所殺，生拘薛泰。

translations.literal: The government army fared poorly; Suogu and Dafu were both killed in battle by Ketuyu, and Xue Tai was captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: The government army was defeated. Suogu and Dafu were both killed in battle by Ketuyu, and Xue Tai was taken alive.

sentences.zh: 營府震恐，許欽澹移軍西入渝關。

translations.literal: The frontier command was shaken with fear, and Xu Qindan moved his army west into Yuguans.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier command was shaken with fear, and Xu Qindan withdrew his army west into Yuguans.

sentences.zh: 可突於立娑固從父弟郁于爲主。

translations.literal: Ketuyu installed Suogu's younger cousin Yuyu as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Ketuyu installed Suogu's younger cousin Yuyu as ruler.

sentences.zh: 俄又遣使請罪，上乃令冊立郁於，令襲娑固官爵，仍赦可突於之罪。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he again sent envoys to plead guilty; the emperor then ordered Yuyu invested, commanded him to inherit Suogu's offices and titles, and still pardoned Ketuyu's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Ketuyu again sent envoys to plead guilty. The emperor then invested Yuyu, ordered him to inherit Suogu's offices and titles, and still pardoned Ketuyu's crimes.

sentences.zh: 十年，郁於入朝請婚。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Yuyu came to court to request marriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Yuyu came to court to request a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 上又封從妹夫率更令慕容嘉賓女爲燕郡公主以妻之，仍封郁於爲松漠郡王，授左金吾衛員外大將軍、兼靜析軍經略大使，賜物千段。

translations.literal: The emperor also enfeoffed the daughter of Murong Jiabin, Rate Supervisor of the Palace and husband of a younger cousin, as Princess of Yancheng Commandery and gave her to him in marriage; he still enfeoffed Yuyu as Prince of Songmo Commandery, appointed him Supernumerary Grand General of the Left Golden Crow Guard and concurrently Commissioner for the Jingxi Army, and bestowed a thousand rolls of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also enfeoffed the daughter of Murong Jiabin, Rate Supervisor of the Palace and husband of a younger cousin, as Princess of Yancheng Commandery and gave her to Yuyu in marriage. Yuyu was further enfeoffed as Prince of Songmo Commandery, appointed Supernumerary Grand General of the Left Golden Crow Guard and Commissioner for the Jingxi Army, and granted a thousand rolls of goods.

sentences.zh: 郁於還蕃，可突於來朝，拜左羽林將軍，從幸并州。

translations.literal: Yuyu returned to his realm; Ketuyu came to court, was appointed General of the Left Feathered Forest Guard, and accompanied the emperor on a visit to Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuyu returned to his realm. Ketuyu came to court, was appointed General of the Left Feathered Forest Guard, and accompanied the emperor to Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，郁於病死，弟吐于代統其衆，襲兄官爵，復以燕郡公主爲妻。

translations.literal: The next year Yuyu died of illness; his younger brother Tuyu succeeded to command of his host, inherited his elder brother's offices and titles, and again took the Princess of Yancheng Commandery as wife.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Yuyu died of illness. His younger brother Tuyu succeeded to command of his people, inherited his brother's offices and titles, and again took the Princess of Yancheng Commandery as his wife.

sentences.zh: 吐于與可突於復相猜阻。

translations.literal: Tuyu and Ketuyu again mutually suspected and obstructed each other.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyu and Ketuyu again grew mutually suspicious and obstructive.

sentences.zh: 十三年，攜公主來奔，便不敢還，改封遼陽郡王，因留宿衛。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he brought the princess and came to flee; he then dared not return, was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Liaoyang Commandery, and was therefore kept in residence as palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Tuyu fled to the court with the princess. He then dared not return and was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Liaoyang Commandery, and was kept at court as a palace guard.

sentences.zh: 可突于立李盡忠弟邵固爲主。

translations.literal: Ketuyu installed Li Jinzhong's younger brother Shaogu as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Ketuyu installed Li Jinzhong's younger brother Shaogu as ruler.

sentences.zh: 其冬，車駕東巡，邵固詣行在所，因從至嶽下，拜左羽林軍員外大將軍、靜析軍經略大使，改封廣化郡王，又封皇從外甥女陳氏爲東華公主以妻之。

translations.literal: That winter, when the imperial carriage toured east, Shaogu came to the temporary palace and accompanied the emperor to the foot of the sacred peak; he was appointed Supernumerary Grand General of the Left Feathered Forest Guard and Commissioner for the Jingxi Army, re-enfeoffed as Prince of Guanghua Commandery, and a younger clanswoman of the emperor, the Lady Chen, was enfeoffed as Princess Donghua and given to him in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when the emperor toured east, Shaogu came to the temporary palace and accompanied him to the foot of the sacred peak. He was appointed Supernumerary Grand General of the Left Feathered Forest Guard and Commissioner for the Jingxi Army, re-enfeoffed as Prince of Guanghua Commandery, and the emperor's younger clanswoman Lady Chen was enfeoffed as Princess Donghua and given to him in marriage.

sentences.zh: 邵固還蕃，又遣可突於入朝，貢方物，中書侍郎李元紘不禮焉，可突於怏怏而去。

translations.literal: Shaogu returned to his realm and again sent Ketuyu to court with tribute goods; Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Yuanhong did not treat him with courtesy, and Ketuyu departed discontented.
translations.idiomatic: Shaogu returned to his realm and again sent Ketuyu to court with tribute goods. Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Yuanhong treated him discourteously, and Ketuyu left in discontent.

sentences.zh: 左丞相張說謂人曰：「兩蕃必叛。

translations.literal: Left Chancellor Zhang Yue said to others: "The two tribes will surely rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Left Chancellor Zhang Yue said to others, "The two tribes will surely rebel.

sentences.zh: 可突於人面獸心，唯利是視，執其國政，人心附之，若不優禮縻之，必不來矣！」

translations.literal: Ketuyu has a human face but a beast's heart; he looks only to profit, holds the government of his state, and the people's hearts attach to him. If he is not treated with generous courtesy to tether him, he will surely not come again!
translations.idiomatic: Ketuyu has a human face but a beast's heart. He looks only to profit, holds the government of his state, and the people are attached to him. Unless he is treated with generous courtesy to keep him bound, he will surely not come again!

sentences.zh: 十八年，可突于殺邵固，率部落並脅奚衆降於突厥，東華公主走投平盧軍。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Ketuyu killed Shaogu, led his tribe and also coerced the Xi host to submit to the Turks, and Princess Donghua fled in distress to the Pinglu Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Ketuyu killed Shaogu, led his tribe and coerced the Xi host to submit to the Turks, and Princess Donghua fled in distress to the Pinglu Army.

sentences.zh: 於是詔中書舍人襲寬、給事中薛侃等於京城及關內、河東、河南、河北分道募壯勇之士，以忠王浚爲河北道行軍元帥以討之，師竟不行。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered Secretariat Draftsmen Xi Kuan, Supervising Secretary Xue Kan, and others to recruit stalwart warriors in the capital and in Guannei, Hedong, Henan, and Hebei along separate routes; Prince Zhong Li Jun was made Grand Commander of the Hebei Circuit campaigning army to attack them, but the army in the end was not dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict ordered Secretariat Draftsmen Xi Kuan, Supervising Secretary Xue Kan, and others to recruit stalwart warriors in the capital and in Guannei, Hedong, Henan, and Hebei along separate routes. Prince Zhong Li Jun was made Grand Commander of the Hebei campaigning army to attack them, but the army was never dispatched.

sentences.zh: 二十年，詔禮部尚書信安王禕爲行軍副大總管，領衆與幽州長史趙含章出塞擊破之，俘獲甚衆。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, an edict appointed Minister of Rites Prince Xin'an Li Yi as Deputy Grand Commander of the campaigning army; he led his host together with Youzhou Chief Administrator Zhao Hanzhang out beyond the passes and defeated them, capturing a great many.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year an edict appointed Minister of Rites Prince Xin'an Li Yi as Deputy Grand Commander of the campaigning army. He led his forces with Youzhou Chief Administrator Zhao Hanzhang beyond the passes, defeated the enemy, and took a great many captives.

sentences.zh: 可突於率其麾下遠遁，奚衆盡降，禕乃班師。

translations.literal: Ketuyu led his personal followers in flight far away; the Xi host all submitted; Yi then withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Ketuyu fled far away with his personal followers. The Xi host all submitted, and Yi then withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 明年，可突於又來抄掠。

translations.literal: The next year Ketuyu again came raiding.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Ketuyu raided the frontier again.

sentences.zh: 幽州長史薛楚玉遣副將郭英傑、吳克勤、鄔知義、羅守忠率精騎萬人，並領降奚之衆追擊之。

translations.literal: Youzhou Chief Administrator Xue Chuyu dispatched Deputy Generals Guo Yingjie, Wu Keqin, Wu Zhiyi, and Luo Shouzhong to lead ten thousand elite cavalry, and also to lead the submitted Xi host in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou Chief Administrator Xue Chuyu dispatched Deputy Generals Guo Yingjie, Wu Keqin, Wu Zhiyi, and Luo Shouzhong to lead ten thousand elite cavalry, together with submitted Xi forces, in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 軍至渝關都山之下，可突於領突厥兵以拒官軍。

translations.literal: When the army reached below Dushan at Yuguans, Ketuyu led Turk troops to resist the government army.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Dushan below Yuguans, Ketuyu led Turk troops to resist the government forces.

sentences.zh: 奚衆遂持兩端，散走保險。

translations.literal: The Xi host then wavered between two sides and scattered, fleeing to fortified places.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi host then wavered between the two sides and scattered, fleeing to fortified terrain.

sentences.zh: 官軍大敗，知義、守忠率麾下遁歸，英傑、克勤沒於陣，其下六千餘人，盡爲賊所殺。

translations.literal: The government army suffered a great defeat; Zhiyi and Shouzhong led their personal followers in flight back, while Yingjie and Keqin perished in battle; more than six thousand men under them were all killed by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The government army was routed. Zhiyi and Shouzhong fled back with their personal followers, while Yingjie and Keqin died in battle. More than six thousand of their men were killed by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 詔以張守珪爲幽州長史兼御史中丞以經略之。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Zhang Shougui Youzhou Chief Administrator and concurrently Censor-in-Chief to manage the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Zhang Shougui Youzhou Chief Administrator and concurrently Censor-in-Chief to manage the frontier.

sentences.zh: 可突於漸爲守珪所逼，遣使偽降。

translations.literal: Ketuyu was gradually pressed by Shougui and sent envoys in feigned submission.
translations.idiomatic: Ketuyu was gradually pressed by Shougui and sent envoys in feigned submission.

sentences.zh: 俄又回惑不定，引衆漸向西北，將就突厥。

translations.literal: Soon he again wavered uncertainly, leading his host gradually toward the northwest, about to join the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he wavered again, leading his people gradually northwest toward the Turks.

sentences.zh: 守珪遣管記王悔等就部落招諭之。

translations.literal: Shougui dispatched Recorder Wang Hui and others to the tribe to summon and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Shougui dispatched Recorder Wang Hui and others to the tribe to summon and instruct them.

sentences.zh: 時契丹衙官李過折與可突於分掌兵馬，情不葉，悔潛誘之，過折夜勒兵斬可突于及其支黨數十人。

translations.literal: At the time Khitan yamen officer Li Guozhe and Ketuyu divided command of troops and horses; their feelings were not in accord; Hui secretly incited him, and Guozhe by night mobilized troops and beheaded Ketuyu and several tens of his partisans.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Khitan yamen officer Li Guozhe and Ketuyu shared command of troops and horses but were not of one mind. Hui secretly won Guozhe over, and Guozhe mobilized troops by night and beheaded Ketuyu and several tens of his partisans.

sentences.zh: 二十三年正月，傳首東都。
