translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-third year, his head was sent to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-third year his head was sent to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 詔封過折爲北平郡王，授特進，檢校松漠州都督，賜錦衣一副、銀器十事、絹彩三千疋。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed Guozhe as Prince of Beiping Commandery, appointed him Special Advancement, made him Inspector of Songmo Prefecture, and bestowed a set of brocade robes, ten items of silverware, and three thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: An edict enfeoffed Guozhe as Prince of Beiping Commandery, appointed him Special Advancement and Inspector of Songmo Prefecture, and bestowed a set of brocade robes, ten pieces of silverware, and three thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 其年，過折爲可突於餘黨泥禮所殺，並其諸子，唯一子刺乾走投安東得免，拜左驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: That year Guozhe was killed by Nili, a remnant partisan of Ketuyu, together with all his sons; only one son, Cigan, fled to Andong and escaped, and was appointed General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: That year Guozhe was killed by Nili, a remnant partisan of Ketuyu, along with all his sons. Only one son, Cigan, fled to Andong and escaped; he was appointed General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 天寶十年，安祿山誣其酋長欲叛，請舉兵討之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tianbao, An Lushan falsely accused their chieftains of intending rebellion and requested troops to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Tianbao, An Lushan falsely accused their chieftains of intending rebellion and requested permission to raise troops against them.

sentences.zh: 八月，以幽州、雲中、平盧之衆數萬人，就潢水南契丹衙與之戰，祿山大敗而還，死者數千人。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, with several tens of thousands of troops from Youzhou, Yunzhong, and Pinglu, he fought them at the Khitan yamen south of the Huangshui River; Lushan was defeated and returned, and several thousand men died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he fought them at the Khitan yamen south of the Huangshui River with several tens of thousands of troops from Youzhou, Yunzhong, and Pinglu. Lushan was defeated and withdrew, and several thousand men were killed.

sentences.zh: 至十二年，又降附。

translations.literal: By the twelfth year they again submitted.
translations.idiomatic: By the twelfth year they submitted again.

sentences.zh: 迄于貞元，常間歲來修籓禮。

translations.literal: Down to the Zhenyuan era they regularly came every other year to observe tributary rites.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the Zhenyuan era they regularly came every other year to observe tributary rites.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年，與奚衆同寇我振武，大掠人畜而去。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan, together with the Xi host they raided our Zhenwu, plundering people and livestock on a great scale before departing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan they joined the Xi in raiding Zhenwu, plundering people and livestock on a large scale before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 九年、十年，復遣使來朝，大首領悔落拽何已下，各授官放還。

translations.literal: In the ninth and tenth years they again sent envoys to court; great chieftains from Huiluozhuaihe downward were each granted offices and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth and tenth years they again sent envoys to court. Great chieftains from Huiluozhuaihe downward were each granted offices and sent back.

sentences.zh: 十一年，大首領熱蘇等二十五人來朝。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year great chieftains Resu and twenty-five others came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year great chieftains Resu and twenty-five others came to court.

sentences.zh: 自後至元和、長慶、寶曆、太和、開成時遣使來朝貢。

translations.literal: From then until the Yuanhe, Changqing, Baoli, Taihe, and Kaicheng eras they sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: From then through the Yuanhe, Changqing, Baoli, Taihe, and Kaicheng eras they sent envoys to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 會昌二年九月，制：「契丹新立王屈戍，可雲麾將軍，守右武衛將軍員外置同正員。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Huichang, ninth month, an edict stated: "Qushu, newly installed king of the Khitan, may be Cloud Banner General and keep Supernumerary Right Martial Guard General with regular commissioner rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huichang, ninth month, an edict stated, "Qushu, newly installed king of the Khitan, is appointed Cloud Banner General and Supernumerary Right Martial Guard General with regular commissioner rank.

sentences.zh: 幽州節度使張仲武上言：「屈戍等雲，契丹舊用回紇印，今懇請聞奏，乞國家賜印。」

translations.literal: Youzhou Military Commissioner Zhang Zhongwu memorialized: "Qushu and others report that the Khitan formerly used Uyghur seals; they now earnestly request that this be reported to the throne and beg the state to bestow a seal.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou Military Commissioner Zhang Zhongwu memorialized, "Qushu and others report that the Khitan formerly used Uyghur seals. They now earnestly request that this be reported to the throne and ask the state to bestow a seal.

sentences.zh: 許之，以「奉國契丹之印」爲文。

translations.literal: This was granted; the inscription read "Seal of the Khitan who serve the State."
translations.idiomatic: This was granted, with the inscription "Seal of the Khitan who serve the State."

sentences.zh: 奚國，蓋匈奴之別種也，所居亦鮮卑故地，即東胡之界也，在京師東北四千餘里。

translations.literal: The Xi state was probably a separate branch of the Xiongnu; they also dwelt in the former Xianbei lands, on the borders of the Eastern Hu, more than four thousand li northeast of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi were probably a separate branch of the Xiongnu. They also lived in the former Xianbei lands, on the borders of the Eastern Hu, more than four thousand li northeast of the capital.

sentences.zh: 東接契丹，西至突厥，南拒白狼河，北至霫國。

translations.literal: East they adjoined the Khitan, west they reached the Turks, south they faced the Bailang River, and north they reached the Xi state.
translations.idiomatic: To the east they bordered the Khitan, to the west the Turks, to the south the Bailang River, and to the north the Xi state.

sentences.zh: 自營州西北饒樂水以至其國。

translations.literal: From northwest of Yingzhou at the Raole River up to their state.
translations.idiomatic: Their territory extended from the Raole River northwest of Yingzhou to their own lands.

sentences.zh: 勝兵三萬餘人，分爲五部，每部置俟斤一人。

translations.literal: Fighting men numbered more than thirty thousand; they were divided into five divisions, each division having one irkin.
translations.idiomatic: They had more than thirty thousand fighting men, divided into five divisions, each with one irkin.

sentences.zh: 風俗並於突厥。

translations.literal: Customs were entirely like those of the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs were entirely like those of the Turks.

sentences.zh: 每隨逐水草，以畜牧爲業，遷徙無常。

translations.literal: They constantly followed water and grass, making livestock their occupation, with no fixed migrations.
translations.idiomatic: They constantly followed pasture and water, lived by herding, and moved without fixed settlements.

sentences.zh: 居有氈帳，兼用車爲營，牙中常五百人持兵自衛。

translations.literal: In residence they had felt tents and also used carts to make camps; in the yurt five hundred men constantly bearing arms guarded themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They lived in felt tents and also used carts to form camps. Five hundred armed men constantly guarded the yurt.

sentences.zh: 此外部落皆散居山谷，無賦稅。

translations.literal: Beyond this the tribes all lived scattered in valleys, without taxes and levies.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond this the tribes all lived scattered in valleys and paid no taxes or levies.

sentences.zh: 其人善射獵，好與契丹戰爭。

translations.literal: Their people were skilled at shooting and hunting and delighted in fighting the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: They were skilled at archery and hunting and delighted in fighting the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 武德中，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the Wude era they sent envoys with tribute to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wude era they sent envoys to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二十二年，酋長可度者率其所部內屬，乃置饒樂都督府，以可度者爲右領軍兼饒樂都督，封樓煩縣公，賜姓李氏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Zhenguan, chieftain Keduzhe led his division to submit internally; the Raole Protectorate was then established, with Keduzhe as Right Army Commander and concurrently Protector of Raole, enfeoffed as Duke of Loufan County, and granted the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Zhenguan chieftain Keduzhe led his division to submit. The Raole Protectorate was then established, with Keduzhe as Right Army Commander and Protector of Raole, enfeoffed as Duke of Loufan County, and granted the surname Li.

sentences.zh: 顯慶初，又授右監門大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianqing he was again appointed Grand General of the Right Gate Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xianqing he was again appointed Grand General of the Right Gate Guard.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天年，契丹叛後，奚衆管屬突厥，兩國常遞爲表裏，號曰「兩蕃」。

translations.literal: In the Wansui Tongtian years, after the Khitan rebelled, the Xi host came under Turk administration; the two states constantly took turns as outer and inner allies and were called "the two tribes."
translations.idiomatic: In the Wansui Tongtian years, after the Khitan rebelled, the Xi came under Turk control. The two peoples regularly acted as outer and inner allies and were called "the two tribes."

sentences.zh: 景雲元年，其首領李大輔遣使貢方物，睿宗嘉之，宴賜甚厚。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyun their chieftain Li Dafu sent envoys with tribute goods; Ruizong was pleased and feasted and rewarded them very generously.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingyun their chieftain Li Dafu sent envoys with tribute goods. Ruizong was pleased and feasted and rewarded them very generously.

sentences.zh: 開元三年，大輔遣其大臣粵蘇梅落來請降，詔復立其地爲饒樂州，封大輔爲饒樂郡王，仍拜左金吾員外大將軍、饒樂州都督。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaiyuan, Dafu sent his senior minister Yuesu Meiluo to request submission; an edict restored their land as Raole Prefecture, enfeoffed Dafu as Prince of Raole Commandery, and also appointed him Supernumerary Grand General of the Left Golden Crow Guard and Protector of Raole Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaiyuan Dafu sent his senior minister Yuesu Meiluo to request submission. An edict restored their lands as Raole Prefecture, enfeoffed Dafu as Prince of Raole Commandery, and appointed him Supernumerary Grand General of the Left Golden Crow Guard and Protector of Raole Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 五年，大輔與契丹首領松漠郡王李失活咸請于柳城依舊置營州都督府，上從之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Dafu and Khitan chieftain Prince of Songmo Commandery Li Shihuo together requested that at Liucheng the former Yingzhou Protectorate be re-established; the emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Dafu and Khitan chieftain Prince of Songmo Commandery Li Shihuo together requested that the Yingzhou Protectorate be re-established at Liucheng as before. The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 敕太子詹事姜師度充使督工作，役八千餘人。

translations.literal: It was ordered that Crown Prince Household Steward Jiang Shidu serve as commissioner to supervise the work, employing more than eight thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Household Steward Jiang Shidu was ordered to serve as commissioner supervising the work, with more than eight thousand men employed.

sentences.zh: 其年，大輔入朝，詔封從外甥女辛氏爲固安公主以妻之，賜物一千五百疋，遣右領軍將軍李濟持節送還蕃。

translations.literal: That year Dafu came to court; an edict enfeoffed a younger clanswoman of the emperor, the Lady Xin, as Princess Guo'an and gave her to him in marriage, bestowed fifteen hundred bolts of goods, and dispatched Right Army Commander General Li Ji bearing credentials to escort him back to his realm.
translations.idiomatic: That year Dafu came to court. An edict enfeoffed a younger clanswoman of the emperor, Lady Xin, as Princess Guo'an and gave her to him in marriage, granted fifteen hundred bolts of goods, and dispatched Right Army Commander General Li Ji bearing credentials to escort him back to his realm.

sentences.zh: 八年，大輔率兵救契丹，戰死，其弟魯蘇嗣立。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Dafu led troops to rescue the Khitan and died in battle; his younger brother Lusu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Dafu led troops to rescue the Khitan and died in battle. His younger brother Lusu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 十年，入朝，詔令襲其兄饒樂郡王、右金吾員外大將軍、兼保塞軍經略大使，賜物一千段，仍以固安公主爲妻。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he came to court; an edict ordered him to inherit his elder brother's Prince of Raole Commandery, Supernumerary Grand General of the Right Golden Crow Guard, and concurrently Commissioner for the Baosai Army, bestowed a thousand rolls of goods, and still took Princess Guo'an as wife.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he came to court. An edict ordered him to inherit his brother's titles as Prince of Raole Commandery, Supernumerary Grand General of the Right Golden Crow Guard, and Commissioner for the Baosai Army, granted a thousand rolls of goods, and again took Princess Guo'an as his wife.

sentences.zh: 而公主與嫡母未和，遞相論告，詔令離婚，復以成安公主之女韋氏爲東光公主以妻之。

translations.literal: But the princess and her legitimate mother-in-law were not on good terms and repeatedly accused each other; an edict ordered divorce, and again the daughter of Princess Cheng'an, the Lady Wei, was enfeoffed as Princess Dongguang and given to him in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: But the princess and her legitimate mother-in-law were not on good terms and repeatedly accused each other. An edict ordered divorce, and the daughter of Princess Cheng'an, Lady Wei, was enfeoffed as Princess Dongguang and given to him in marriage.

sentences.zh: 十四年，又改封魯蘇爲奉誠王，授右羽林軍員外將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Lusu was again re-enfeoffed as Prince of Fengcheng and appointed Supernumerary General of the Right Feathered Forest Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Lusu was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Fengcheng and appointed Supernumerary General of the Right Feathered Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 十八年，奚衆爲契丹衙官可突於所脅，復叛降突厥。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Xi host was coerced by Khitan yamen officer Ketuyu and again rebelled and submitted to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the Xi were coerced by Khitan yamen officer Ketuyu and again rebelled and submitted to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 魯蘇不能制，走投渝關，東光公主奔歸平盧軍。

translations.literal: Lusu could not control them and fled in distress to Yuguans; Princess Dongguang fled back to the Pinglu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Lusu could not control them and fled in distress to Yuguans. Princess Dongguang fled back to the Pinglu Army.

sentences.zh: 其秋，幽州長史趙含章發清夷軍兵擊奚。

translations.literal: That autumn Youzhou Chief Administrator Zhao Hanzhang dispatched Qingyi Army troops to attack the Xi.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Youzhou Chief Administrator Zhao Hanzhang dispatched Qingyi Army troops to attack the Xi.

sentences.zh: 破之，斬首二百級。

translations.literal: He defeated them and took two hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated them and took two hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 自是奚衆稍稍歸降。

translations.literal: From this the Xi host gradually returned in submission.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Xi gradually returned in submission.

sentences.zh: 二十年，信安王禕奉詔討叛奚。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Prince Xin'an Li Yi received an edict to attack the rebellious Xi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Prince Xin'an Li Yi received an edict to attack the rebellious Xi.

sentences.zh: 奚酋長李詩、瑣高等以其部落五千帳來降。

translations.literal: Xi chieftains Li Shi and Suogao led their tribes, five thousand tents, to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Xi chieftains Li Shi and Suogao led their tribes, five thousand tents, to submit.

sentences.zh: 詔封李詩爲歸義王、兼特進、左羽林軍大將軍同正。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed Li Shi as Prince of Guiyi, concurrently Special Advancement, and Left Feathered Forest Guard Grand General with regular rank.
translations.idiomatic: An edict enfeoffed Li Shi as Prince of Guiyi, concurrently Special Advancement, and Left Feathered Forest Guard Grand General with regular rank.

sentences.zh: 仍充歸義州都督，賜物十萬段，移其部落於幽州界安置。

translations.literal: He was also made Protector of Guiyi Prefecture, bestowed one hundred thousand rolls of goods, and their tribes were moved and settled on the borders of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Protector of Guiyi Prefecture, granted one hundred thousand rolls of goods, and their tribes were resettled on the borders of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 天寶五載，又封其王娑固爲昭信王，仍授饒樂都督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianbao their king Suogu was again enfeoffed as Prince of Zhaoxin and still appointed Protector of Raole.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianbao their king Suogu was again enfeoffed as Prince of Zhaoxin and appointed Protector of Raole.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遣使獻名馬。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year they sent envoys presenting famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year they sent envoys presenting famous horses.

sentences.zh: 爾後每歲朝貢不絕，或歲中二三至。

translations.literal: Thereafter tribute missions each year were unceasing, sometimes two or three in a year.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they sent tribute every year without fail, sometimes two or three missions in a single year.

sentences.zh: 故事，常以范陽節度使爲押奚、契丹兩蕃使。

translations.literal: By precedent the Fanyang Military Commissioner was regularly made Commissioner for the Xi and Khitan, the two tribes.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the Fanyang Military Commissioner was regularly made Commissioner for the Xi and Khitan, the two tribes.

sentences.zh: 自至德之後，籓臣多擅封壤，朝廷優容之，彼務自完，不生邊事，故二蕃亦少爲寇。

translations.literal: From after the Zhide era frontier ministers mostly usurped their territories; the court indulged them, and they sought their own preservation and did not raise border incidents, so the two tribes also raided little.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhide era frontier governors mostly usurped their own territories. The court indulged them, and they sought self-preservation rather than border trouble, so the two tribes also raided little.

sentences.zh: 其每歲朝賀，常各遣數百人至幽州，則選其酋渠三五十人赴闕，引見於麟德殿，錫以金帛遣還，餘皆駐而館之，率爲常也。

translations.literal: Each year when they came for court congratulations, they regularly each sent several hundred men to Youzhou; then thirty to fifty of their chieftains were selected to go to the palace, received audience in Qinde Hall, granted gold and silk and sent back—the rest all stayed and were lodged; this became the regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: Each year for court congratulations they regularly sent several hundred men each to Youzhou. Then thirty to fifty of their chieftains were selected to go to the capital, received audience in Qinde Hall, granted gold and silk, and sent back, while the rest remained lodged there. This became the regular practice.

sentences.zh: 室韋者，契丹之別類也。

translations.literal: The Shiwei were a separate branch of the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: The Shiwei were a separate branch of the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 居峱越河北，其國在京師東北七千里。

translations.literal: They dwelt north of the Nao River; their state was seven thousand li northeast of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: They lived north of the Nao River, seven thousand li northeast of the capital.

sentences.zh: 東至黑水靺鞨，西至突厥，南接契丹，北至於海。

translations.literal: East to the Heishui Mohe, west to the Turks, south adjoining the Khitan, north reaching the sea.
translations.idiomatic: To the east lay the Heishui Mohe, to the west the Turks, to the south the Khitan, and to the north the sea.

sentences.zh: 其國無君長，有大首領十七人，並號「莫賀弗」，世管攝之，而附於突厥。

translations.literal: Their state had no sovereign; there were seventeen great chieftains, all styled "Mohefu," who managed affairs by hereditary succession, and they were attached to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Their state had no single ruler. Seventeen great chieftains, all styled "Mohefu," managed affairs by hereditary succession, and they were attached to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 兵器有角弓楛矢，尤善射，時聚弋獵，事畢而散。

translations.literal: Their weapons included horn bows and oak arrows; they were especially skilled at shooting; they would gather for hunting and then disperse when finished.
translations.idiomatic: Their weapons included horn bows and oak arrows. They were especially skilled at archery, gathering for hunts and dispersing when finished.

sentences.zh: 其人土著，無賦斂。

translations.literal: Their people were sedentary, without taxes and levies.
translations.idiomatic: They were sedentary and paid no taxes or levies.

sentences.zh: 或爲小室，以皮覆上，相聚而居，至數十百家。

translations.literal: Sometimes they made small dwellings covered with hides, living gathered together, up to several tens or hundreds of households.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes they built small dwellings covered with hides and lived together in settlements of several tens or hundreds of households.

sentences.zh: 剡木爲犁，不加金刃，人牽以種，不解用牛。

translations.literal: They carved wood into ploughs without adding metal blades; men pulled them to sow and did not know how to use oxen.
translations.idiomatic: They carved wooden ploughs without metal blades, pulled them by hand to sow, and did not know how to use oxen.

sentences.zh: 夏多霧雨，冬多霜霰。

translations.literal: In summer there was much fog and rain; in winter much frost and hail.
translations.idiomatic: Summers brought much fog and rain; winters brought much frost and hail.

sentences.zh: 畜宜犬豕，豢養而啖之，其皮用以爲韋，男子女人通以爲服。

translations.literal: Dogs and pigs were suitable livestock; they were raised and eaten, their hides used for leather, and men and women alike wore them as clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Dogs and pigs were their main livestock. They raised and ate them, used the hides for leather, and men and women alike wore them as clothing.

sentences.zh: 被髮左衽，其家富者項著五色雜珠。

translations.literal: They wore their hair loose and folded the lapel to the left; in wealthy families people wore multi-colored beads at the neck.
translations.idiomatic: They wore their hair loose and folded their lapels to the left. Wealthy families wore multi-colored beads at the neck.

sentences.zh: 婚嫁之法，男先就女舍，三年役力，因得親迎其婦。

translations.literal: For marriage custom, the man first went to the woman's house, serving with his strength for three years, and thereby could personally welcome his bride.
translations.idiomatic: In marriage custom the man first went to the woman's house and served with his labor for three years, after which he could personally welcome his bride.

sentences.zh: 役日已滿，女家分其財物，夫婦同車而載，鼓舞共歸。

translations.literal: When the term of service was fulfilled, the woman's family divided their property; husband and wife rode in the same cart, drumming and dancing together as they returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the term of service was fulfilled, the woman's family divided their property. Husband and wife rode in the same cart, drumming and dancing together as they returned home.

sentences.zh: 武德中，獻方物。

translations.literal: In the Wude era they presented tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wude era they presented tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，遣使貢豐貂，自此朝貢不絕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan they sent envoys presenting sable furs; from then tribute missions were unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenguan they sent envoys presenting sable furs. From then on their tribute missions never ceased.

sentences.zh: 又云：室韋，我唐有九部焉。

translations.literal: It is also recorded: the Shiwei—our Tang had nine divisions of them.
translations.idiomatic: It is also recorded that the Shiwei comprised nine divisions under our Tang.

sentences.zh: 所謂嶺西室韋、山北室韋、黃頭室韋、大如者室韋、小如者室韋、婆萵室韋、訥北室韋、駱駝室韋，並在柳城郡之東北，近者三千五百里，遠者六千二百里。

translations.literal: Namely Lingxi Shiwei, Shanbei Shiwei, Huangtou Shiwei, Daruzhe Shiwei, Xiaoruzhe Shiwei, Powo Shiwei, Nebei Shiwei, and Luotuo Shiwei—all were northeast of Liucheng Commandery, the near ones three thousand five hundred li, the far ones six thousand two hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: These were Lingxi Shiwei, Shanbei Shiwei, Huangtou Shiwei, Daruzhe Shiwei, Xiaoruzhe Shiwei, Powo Shiwei, Nebei Shiwei, and Luotuo Shiwei—all northeast of Liucheng Commandery, the nearest three thousand five hundred li away and the farthest six thousand two hundred li.

sentences.zh: 今室韋最西與回紇接界者，烏素固部落，當俱輪泊之西南。

translations.literal: Now among the Shiwei, the westernmost bordering the Huihe is the Wusugu tribe, located southwest of Lake Julun.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Shiwei tribes today, the westernmost one bordering the Huihe is the Wusugu tribe, situated southwest of Lake Julun.

sentences.zh: 次東有移塞沒部落。

translations.literal: Next to the east is the Yisaimo tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Next to the east lies the Yisaimo tribe.

sentences.zh: 次東又有塞曷支部落，此部落有良馬，人戶亦多，居啜河之南，其河彼俗謂之燕支河。

translations.literal: Next to the east again is the Saihebu tribe; this tribe has fine horses and many households, dwelling south of the Chuo River—in their custom that river is called the Yanzhi River.
translations.idiomatic: Farther east is the Saihebu tribe, which has fine horses and a large population. They live south of the Chuo River, which they call the Yanzhi River.

sentences.zh: 次又有和解部落，次東又有烏羅護部落，又有那禮部落。

translations.literal: Next again is the Hejie tribe; next to the east again is the Wuluohu tribe; and again there is the Nali tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Next comes the Hejie tribe, then farther east the Wuluohu tribe, and also the Nali tribe.

sentences.zh: 又東北有山北室韋，又北有小如者室韋，又北有婆萵室韋，東又有嶺西室韋，又東南至黃頭室韋，此部落兵強，人戶亦多，東北與達姤接。

translations.literal: Northeast again is Shanbei Shiwei; north again is Xiaoruzhe Shiwei; north again is Powo Shiwei; east again is Lingxi Shiwei; southeast again is Huangtou Shiwei—this tribe's soldiers are strong and its households many; northeast it adjoins the Dada.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast are the Shanbei Shiwei; farther north the Xiaoruzhe Shiwei and still farther north the Powo Shiwei; to the east the Lingxi Shiwei; and to the southeast the Huangtou Shiwei. The Huangtou tribe is militarily strong and populous, and to the northeast it borders the Dada.

sentences.zh: 嶺西室韋北又有訥北支室韋，此部落較小。

translations.literal: North of Lingxi Shiwei again is Neibeizhi Shiwei; this tribe is comparatively small.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Lingxi Shiwei is the Neibeizhi Shiwei, a comparatively small tribe.

sentences.zh: 烏羅護之東北二百餘里，那河之北有古烏丸之遺人，今亦自稱烏丸國。

translations.literal: Two hundred-odd li northeast of Wuluohu, north of the Na River, are survivors of the ancient Wuhuan; they now also call themselves the state of Wuhuan.
translations.idiomatic: Some two hundred li northeast of Wuluohu, north of the Na River, live the descendants of the ancient Wuhuan, who now also style themselves the state of Wuhuan.

sentences.zh: 武德、貞觀中，亦遣使來朝貢。

translations.literal: In the Wude and Zhenguan eras they also sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wude and Zhenguan eras they also sent envoys to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 其北大山之北有大室韋部落，其部落傍望建河居。

translations.literal: North of the great mountain to their north is the Great Shiwei tribe; that tribe dwells along the Wangjian River.
translations.idiomatic: North of the great mountain range to their north is the Great Shiwei tribe, which lives along the Wangjian River.

sentences.zh: 其河源出突厥東北界俱輪泊，屈曲東流，經西室韋界，又東經大室韋界，又東經蒙兀室韋之北，落俎室韋之南，又東流與那河、忽汗河合，又東經南黑水靺鞨之北，北黑水靺鞨之南，東流注於海。

translations.literal: Its source emerges from Lake Julun on the Turks' northeastern frontier; winding, it flows east, passing through the territory of the Western Shiwei, then east again through the territory of the Great Shiwei, then east again north of the Mengwu Shiwei and south of the Luozu Shiwei; flowing east again it joins the Na River and the Hohan River, then east again passes north of the Southern Heishui Mohe and south of the Northern Heishui Mohe, and flowing east enters the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Its source lies in Lake Julun on the Turks' northeastern frontier. Winding eastward, it passes through Western Shiwei territory and then Great Shiwei territory, running north of the Mengwu Shiwei and south of the Luozu Shiwei. Farther east it joins the Na and Hohan rivers, then flows east between the Southern and Northern Heishui Mohe before emptying into the sea.

sentences.zh: 烏丸東南三百里，又有東室韋部落，在峱越河之北。

translations.literal: Three hundred li southeast of the Wuhuan, again there is the Eastern Shiwei tribe, north of the Nao River.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred li southeast of the Wuhuan is the Eastern Shiwei tribe, north of the Nao River.

sentences.zh: 其河東南流，與那河合。

translations.literal: That river flows southeast and joins the Na River.
translations.idiomatic: That river flows southeast and joins the Na River.

sentences.zh: 開元、天寶間，比年或間歲入貢。

translations.literal: Between the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, they sent tribute every year or every other year.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras they sent tribute annually or every other year.

sentences.zh: 大曆中，亦頻遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the Dali era they also frequently sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali era they also sent tribute envoys frequently.

sentences.zh: 貞元八年閏十二月，室韋都督和解熱素等一十人來朝。

translations.literal: In the intercalary twelfth month of the eighth year of Zhenyuan, Shiwei Protector Hejie Resu and ten others came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary twelfth month of the eighth year of Zhenyuan, Shiwei Protector Hejie Resu and nine others—ten men in all—came to court.

sentences.zh: 太和五年至八年，凡三遣使來。

translations.literal: From the fifth to the eighth year of Taihe, envoys were sent three times in all.
translations.idiomatic: From the fifth through the eighth year of Taihe, they sent envoys three times in all.

sentences.zh: 九年十二月，室韋大都督阿成等三十人來朝。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the ninth year, Great Shiwei Protector Acheng and thirty others came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the ninth year, Great Shiwei Protector Acheng and twenty-nine others—thirty men in all—came to court.

sentences.zh: 開成、會昌中，亦遣使來朝貢不絕。

translations.literal: In the Kaicheng and Huichang eras they also sent envoys to court with tribute without cease.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaicheng and Huichang eras their tribute missions to court likewise never ceased.

sentences.zh: 靺鞨，蓋肅慎之地，後魏謂之勿吉，在京師東北六千餘里。

translations.literal: The Mohe were essentially the land of the Sushen; the Later Wei called them Wuji; they were more than six thousand li northeast of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Mohe occupied the ancient land of the Sushen. The Later Wei called them Wuji, and they lay more than six thousand li northeast of the capital.

sentences.zh: 東至於海，西接突厥，南界高麗，北鄰室韋。

translations.literal: East to the sea, west adjoining the Turks, south bordering Goryeo, north neighboring the Shiwei.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands reached east to the sea, west to the Turks, south to Goryeo, and north to the Shiwei.

sentences.zh: 其國凡爲數十部，各有酋帥，或附於高麗，或臣於突厥。

translations.literal: Their state altogether comprised several tens of divisions, each with its own chieftain; some were attached to Goryeo, some submitted to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Their country was divided into several dozen tribes, each with its own chieftain. Some were attached to Goryeo, others submitted to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 而黑水靺鞨最處北方，尤稱勁捷，每恃其勇，恆爲鄰境之患。

translations.literal: The Heishui Mohe were farthest north and were especially famed for vigor and swiftness; relying on their courage, they constantly became a scourge to neighboring lands.
translations.idiomatic: The Heishui Mohe, farthest to the north, were especially famed for vigor and swiftness. Trusting in their courage, they constantly menaced their neighbors.

sentences.zh: 俗皆編發，性兇悍，無憂戚，貴壯而賤老。

translations.literal: Their custom was to plait the hair; their nature was fierce and brutal; they knew no sorrow or grief; they honored the strong and despised the old.
translations.idiomatic: They plaited their hair by custom. Fierce by nature, they knew little of sorrow and valued strength while despising age.

sentences.zh: 無屋宇，並依山水掘地爲穴，架木於上，以土覆之，狀如中國之塚墓，相聚而居。

translations.literal: They had no houses or halls; all relied on mountains and rivers, digging earth into pits, setting wood above and covering it with soil, shaped like Chinese tombs, living gathered together.
translations.idiomatic: They had no houses. Instead they dug pits into hillsides by mountains and rivers, framed them with timber, and covered them with earth so that they resembled Chinese tombs, living together in clusters.

sentences.zh: 夏則出隨水草，冬則入處穴中。

translations.literal: In summer they went out following grass and water; in winter they entered and dwelt in the pits.
translations.idiomatic: In summer they moved with the grass and water; in winter they returned to their pit dwellings.

sentences.zh: 父子相承，世爲君長。

translations.literal: Father and son succeeded one another, generation after generation serving as lord and chief.
translations.idiomatic: Leadership passed from father to son, each generation serving as tribal chief.

sentences.zh: 俗無文字。

translations.literal: Their custom had no writing.
translations.idiomatic: They had no written language.

sentences.zh: 兵器有角弓及楛矢。

translations.literal: Their weapons included horn bows and oak arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Their weapons included horn bows and oak arrows.

sentences.zh: 其畜宜豬，富人至數百口，食其肉而衣其皮。

translations.literal: Pigs were suitable livestock for them; the wealthy might have several hundred head, eating their meat and wearing their hides.
translations.idiomatic: Pigs were their principal livestock. The wealthy might keep several hundred head, eating the meat and wearing the hides.

sentences.zh: 死者穿地埋之，以身襯土，無棺斂之具，殺所乘馬於屍前設祭。

translations.literal: When someone died they dug earth and buried him, the body padded with soil, without coffin or burial goods; they killed the horse he had ridden and set out offerings before the corpse.
translations.idiomatic: The dead were buried in the earth with the body laid directly against the soil, without coffin or grave goods. They slaughtered the deceased's mount and made offerings before the corpse.

sentences.zh: 有酋帥突地稽者，隋末率其部千餘家內屬，處之于營州，煬帝授突地稽金紫光祿大夫、遼西太守。

translations.literal: There was a chieftain named Tudiji; at the end of the Sui he led more than a thousand households of his division to submit inward, and they were settled at Yingzhou; Emperor Yang appointed Tudiji Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Grandee's Tally and Administrator of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: A chieftain named Tudiji led more than a thousand households of his tribe to submit at the end of the Sui. They were settled at Yingzhou, and Emperor Yang appointed Tudiji Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Grandee's Tally and made him Administrator of Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 武德初，遣間使朝貢，以其部落置燕州，仍以突地稽爲總管。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude he sent secret envoys with tribute; his tribe was established as Yanzhou, and Tudiji was again made Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wude era he sent secret envoys with tribute. His tribe was organized as Yanzhou, and Tudiji was appointed its area commander.

sentences.zh: 劉黑闥之叛也，突地稽率所部赴定州，遣使詣太宗請受節度，以戰功封蓍國公。

translations.literal: When Liu Heita rebelled, Tudiji led his division to Dingzhou, sent envoys to Emperor Taizong requesting to accept military command, and for battle merit was enfeoffed as Duke of Shiguo.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Heita rebelled, Tudiji led his tribe to Dingzhou and sent envoys to Emperor Taizong asking to serve under Tang command. For his military merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Shiguo.

sentences.zh: 又徙其部落於幽州之昌平城。

translations.literal: His tribe was again moved to Changping City in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His tribe was then moved to Changping City in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 會高開道引突厥來攻幽州，突地稽率兵邀擊，大破之。

translations.literal: When Gao Kaidao brought the Turks to attack Youzhou, Tudiji led troops to intercept and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Kaidao brought the Turks to attack Youzhou, Tudiji led troops to intercept them and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，拜右衛將軍，賜姓李氏。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was appointed General of the Right Guard and granted the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenguan era he was appointed General of the Right Guard and granted the surname Li.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 子謹行，偉貌，武力絕人。

translations.literal: His son Jinxing had a imposing appearance and strength surpassing other men.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jinxing was imposing in appearance and possessed extraordinary strength.

sentences.zh: 麟德中，曆遷營州都督。

translations.literal: In the Linde era he successively rose to Protector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Linde era he rose through the ranks to become Protector of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 其部落家僮數千人，以財力雄邊，爲夷人所憚。

translations.literal: His tribe's household retainers numbered several thousand men; by wealth and power he dominated the frontier and was feared by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: His tribe kept several thousand household retainers. With his wealth and power he dominated the frontier, and the frontier peoples feared him.

sentences.zh: 累拜右領軍大將軍，爲積石道經略大使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed Grand General of the Right Inspecting Army and served as Commissioner for Frontier Affairs on the Jishi Route.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand General of the Right Inspecting Army and appointed Commissioner for Frontier Affairs on the Jishi Route.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃論欽陵等率衆十萬人入寇湟中，謹行兵士樵采，素不設備，忽聞賊至，遂建旗伐鼓，開門以待之。

translations.literal: The Tibetan Lun Qinling and others led a host of one hundred thousand men to raid Huangzhong; Jinxing's soldiers were gathering firewood and had never maintained defenses; suddenly hearing the enemy had arrived, he then raised banners, beat drums, and opened the gates to await them.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan Lun Qinling and others led one hundred thousand men to raid Huangzhong. Jinxing's soldiers were out gathering firewood and were wholly unprepared. When they suddenly heard the enemy was upon them, he raised banners, beat drums, and opened the gates to receive them.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃疑有伏兵，竟不敢進。

translations.literal: The Tibetans suspected an ambush and in the end did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans suspected an ambush and in the end did not dare advance.

sentences.zh: 其白山部，素附於高麗，因收平壤之後，部衆多入中國。

translations.literal: The Baishan division had long been attached to Goryeo; after the capture of Pyongyang, many of its people entered China.
translations.idiomatic: The Baishan division had long been attached to Goryeo. After the capture of Pyongyang, many of its people entered Tang territory.

sentences.zh: 汨咄、安居、骨室等部，亦因高麗破後奔散微弱，後無聞焉。

translations.literal: The Mizhu, Anju, Gushi, and other divisions also, after Goryeo's destruction, fled and scattered and grew weak; afterward nothing more was heard of them.
translations.idiomatic: The Mizhu, Anju, Gushi, and other divisions likewise fled and scattered after Goryeo's fall, dwindled away, and were heard from no more.

sentences.zh: 縱有遺人，並爲渤海編戶。

translations.literal: Even if any survivors remained, all became registered households of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Any survivors who remained were enrolled as registered households of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 唯黑水部全盛，分爲十六部，部又以南北爲稱。

translations.literal: Only the Heishui division remained fully flourishing, divided into sixteen divisions; the divisions were again designated by north and south.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Heishui division remained fully flourishing. It was divided into sixteen subdivisions, which were further distinguished as northern and southern.

sentences.zh: 開元十三年，安東都護薛泰請于黑水靺鞨內置黑水軍。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, Protector-General of Andong Xue Tai requested that the Heishui Army be established within the Heishui Mohe.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, Protector-General of Andong Xue Tai requested the establishment of the Heishui Army among the Heishui Mohe.

sentences.zh: 續更以最大部落爲黑水府，仍以其首領爲都督，諸部刺史隸屬焉。

translations.literal: Subsequently the largest tribe was further made the Heishui Prefecture, its chieftain again made Protector, and the prefectural governors of the various divisions were placed under his authority.
translations.idiomatic: The largest tribe was then organized as Heishui Prefecture, its chieftain appointed Protector, and the governors of the various subdivisions placed under his authority.

sentences.zh: 中國置長史，就其部落監領之。

translations.literal: China established a Chief Administrator to supervise and oversee them in their tribe.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed a chief administrator to supervise them in their own territory.

sentences.zh: 十六年，其都督賜姓李氏，名獻誠，授雲麾將軍兼黑水經略使，仍以幽州都督爲其押使，自此朝貢不絕。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year its Protector was granted the surname Li and the name Xiancheng, appointed General of Cloud-like Might and concurrently Commissioner for Frontier Affairs of Heishui; the Protector of Youzhou was again made his supervising commissioner; from then tribute missions were unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year its Protector was granted the surname Li and the name Xiancheng, appointed General of Cloud-like Might and concurrently Commissioner for Frontier Affairs of Heishui, with the Protector of Youzhou as his supervising commissioner. From then on their tribute missions never ceased.

sentences.zh: 渤海靺鞨

translations.literal: Bohai Mohe
translations.idiomatic: Bohai Mohe

sentences.zh: 渤海靺鞨大祚榮者，本高麗別種也。

translations.literal: Dazuorong of the Bohai Mohe was originally a separate branch of Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Dazuorong of the Bohai Mohe was originally a separate branch of the Goryeo people.

sentences.zh: 高麗既滅，祚榮率家屬徙居營州。

translations.literal: Once Goryeo was destroyed, Zuorong led his family and dependents to move and dwell at Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Goryeo was destroyed, Zuorong moved with his family to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天年，契丹李盡忠反叛，祚榮與靺鞨乞四比羽各領亡命東奔，保阻以自固。

translations.literal: In the Wansui Tongtian era, the Khitan Li Jinzhong rebelled; Zuorong and the Mohe Qi Sibi each led fugitives fleeing east, holding defiles to secure themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wansui Tongtian era, when the Khitan Li Jinzhong rebelled, Zuorong and the Mohe chieftain Qi Sibi each led fugitives eastward and held mountain defiles to secure themselves.

sentences.zh: 盡忠既死，則天命右玉鈐衛大將軍李楷固率兵討其餘黨，先破斬乞四比羽，又度天門嶺以迫祚榮。

translations.literal: Once Jinzhong had died, Empress Zetian ordered General of the Right Jade Talisman Guard Li Kaigu to lead troops to suppress the remaining faction; he first defeated and beheaded Qi Sibi, then crossed Tianmen Ridge to press Zuorong.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinzhong's death, Empress Zetian ordered General of the Right Jade Talisman Guard Li Kaigu to lead troops against the remaining rebels. He first defeated and beheaded Qi Sibi, then crossed Tianmen Ridge to press Zuorong.

sentences.zh: 祚榮合高麗、靺鞨之衆以拒楷固；

translations.literal: Zuorong combined the hosts of Goryeo and the Mohe to resist Kaigu;
translations.idiomatic: Zuorong combined Goryeo and Mohe forces to resist Kaigu;

sentences.zh: 王師大敗，楷固脫身而還。

translations.literal: the imperial army was greatly defeated, and Kaigu escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army was routed, and Kaigu escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 屬契丹及奚盡降突厥，道路阻絕，則天不能討，祚榮遂率其衆東保桂婁之故地，據東牟山，築城以居之。

translations.literal: As the Khitan and Xi all submitted to the Turks and the roads were cut off, Zetian could not pursue the campaign; Zuorong then led his host east to hold the former territory of Guiweng, seized Mount Dongmou, and built a city to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan and Xi all submitted to the Turks and the routes were cut off, Zetian could not continue the campaign. Zuorong then led his followers east to the former territory of Guiweng, seized Mount Dongmou, and built a city to dwell in.

sentences.zh: 祚榮驍勇善用兵，靺鞨之衆及高麗餘燼，稍稍歸之。

translations.literal: Zuorong was fierce and brave and skilled in using troops; the Mohe host and the embers of Goryeo gradually came over to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zuorong was fierce, brave, and skilled in war. Mohe tribesmen and the remnants of Goryeo gradually rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 聖曆中，自立爲振國王，遣使通於突厥。

translations.literal: In the Shengli era he declared himself King of Zhen, and sent envoys to communicate with the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shengli era he declared himself King of Zhen and sent envoys to establish contact with the Turks.

sentences.zh: 其地在營州之東二千里，南與新羅相接。

translations.literal: His territory was two thousand li east of Yingzhou, south adjoining Silla.
translations.idiomatic: His territory lay two thousand li east of Yingzhou and bordered Silla to the south.

sentences.zh: 越熹靺鞨東北至黑水靺鞨，地方二千里，編戶十余萬，勝兵數萬人。

translations.literal: From Yuexi Mohe in the northeast to Heishui Mohe, the territory was two thousand li square; registered households numbered more than one hundred thousand, and battle-ready troops several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: From Yuexi Mohe in the northeast to Heishui Mohe, its territory measured two thousand li across. It had more than one hundred thousand registered households and several tens of thousands of fighting men.

sentences.zh: 風俗瑟高麗及契丹同，頗有文字及書記。

translations.literal: Customs were the same as Goryeo and the Khitan; they had considerable writing and record-keeping.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs resembled those of Goryeo and the Khitan, and they had a written language and kept records.

sentences.zh: 開元七年，祚榮死，玄宗遣使弔祭。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kaiyuan Zuorong died, and Emperor Xuanzong sent envoys to offer condolences and sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Kaiyuan, Zuorong died, and Emperor Xuanzong sent envoys to offer condolences and sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 乃冊立其嫡子桂婁郡王大武藝襲父爲左驍衛大將軍、渤海郡王、忽汗州都督。

translations.literal: He then invested his legitimate son, Prince of Guiweng Commandery Dawuyi, to succeed his father as Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard, King of Bohai Commandery, and Protector of Hohan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He then invested Zuorong's legitimate son, Prince Dawuyi of Guiweng Commandery, to succeed his father as Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard, King of Bohai Commandery, and Protector of Hohan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十四年，黑水靺鞨遣使來朝，詔以其地爲黑水州，仍置長史，遣使鎮押。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the Heishui Mohe sent envoys to court; an edict made their land Heishui Prefecture, again established a Chief Administrator, and dispatched envoys to garrison and supervise them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the Heishui Mohe sent envoys to court. An edict organized their territory as Heishui Prefecture, appointed a chief administrator, and dispatched envoys to garrison and supervise them.

sentences.zh: 武藝謂其屬曰：「黑水途經我境，始與唐家相通。

translations.literal: Wuyi said to his followers: "The Heishui route passes through our territory before reaching the Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi told his followers, "The Heishui route passes through our territory before anyone can reach the Tang.

sentences.zh: 舊請突厥吐屯，皆先告我同去。

translations.literal: Formerly when they requested Turkish tutuns, they always informed us first and went together.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, when they sought Turkish tutuns, they always informed us first and went together with us.

sentences.zh: 今不計會，即請漢官，必是與唐家通謀，腹背攻我也。」

translations.literal: Now without consulting us they immediately request Han officials—they must be in secret collusion with the Tang and will attack me from front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: Now they consult us no longer and immediately request Tang officials. They must be in secret collusion with the Tang and plan to attack us from both front and rear.

sentences.zh: 遣母弟大門藝及其舅任雅發兵以擊黑水。

translations.literal: He dispatched his younger brother by the same mother, Da Menyi, and his maternal uncle Ren Ya to raise troops and attack the Heishui Mohe.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched his younger brother Da Menyi and his maternal uncle Ren Ya to raise troops and attack the Heishui Mohe.

sentences.zh: 門藝曾充質子至京師，開元初還國，至是謂武藝曰：「黑水請唐家官史，即欲擊之，是背唐也。

translations.literal: Menyi had once served as hostage at the capital; at the beginning of Kaiyuan he returned to his state, and on this occasion said to Wuyi: "The Heishui have requested Tang officials, and you immediately wish to attack them—that is turning against the Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Menyi had once served as a hostage at the capital and returned home at the beginning of the Kaiyuan era. On this occasion he told Wuyi, "The Heishui have requested Tang officials, and you wish at once to attack them. That means turning against the Tang.

sentences.zh: 唐國人衆兵強，萬倍於我，一朝結怨，但自取滅亡。

translations.literal: The Tang state has multitudes of people and strong armies, ten thousand times our strength; once enmity is joined, we will only bring destruction upon ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang has vast numbers and mighty armies, ten thousand times our strength. Once we incur their enmity, we will only bring destruction upon ourselves.

sentences.zh: 昔高麗全盛之時，強兵三十余萬，抗敵唐家，不事賓伏，唐兵一臨，掃地俱盡。

translations.literal: Formerly when Goryeo was in full flourishing, with strong troops of more than three hundred thousand resisting the Tang and refusing submission, once Tang troops arrived all were swept away to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When Goryeo was at its height it had more than three hundred thousand strong troops and resisted the Tang without submitting. Yet once Tang armies arrived, everything was swept away.

sentences.zh: 今日渤海之衆，數倍少於高麗，乃欲違背唐家，事必不可。」

translations.literal: Today Bohai's host is several times fewer than Goryeo's; yet you wish to defy the Tang—the thing absolutely cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Bohai's forces today are several times smaller than Goryeo's at its peak, yet you wish to defy the Tang. Such a course is absolutely impossible."

sentences.zh: 武藝不從。

translations.literal: Wuyi would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi would not listen.

sentences.zh: 門藝兵至境，又上書固諫。

translations.literal: When Menyi's troops reached the border, he again submitted a memorial firmly remonstrating.
translations.idiomatic: When Menyi's troops reached the border, he submitted another memorial firmly remonstrating.

sentences.zh: 武藝怒，遣從兄大壹夏代門藝統兵，征門藝，欲殺之。

translations.literal: Wuyi grew angry, dispatched his older clansman Da Yixia to replace Menyi in command of the troops, and marched against Menyi intending to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi grew angry and dispatched his older clansman Da Yixia to replace Menyi in command of the army, then marched against Menyi intending to kill him.

sentences.zh: 門藝遂棄其衆，間道來奔，詔授左驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: Menyi then abandoned his host, came fleeing by a hidden route, and was appointed by edict General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Menyi then abandoned his troops, fled by a hidden route, and was appointed by edict General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 武藝尋遣使朝貢，仍上表極言門藝罪狀，請殺之。

translations.literal: Wuyi soon sent envoys with tribute and also submitted a memorial fully stating Menyi's crimes, requesting that he be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi soon sent tribute envoys and submitted a memorial detailing Menyi's crimes, asking that he be executed.

sentences.zh: 上密遣門藝往安西，仍報武藝云：「門藝遠來歸投，義不可殺。

translations.literal: The emperor secretly dispatched Menyi to Anxi and still replied to Wuyi saying: "Menyi came from afar to submit; by right he cannot be killed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly sent Menyi to Anxi and replied to Wuyi, "Menyi came from afar to submit. By every principle of justice he cannot be killed.

sentences.zh: 今流向嶺南，已遣去訖。」

translations.literal: He is now being sent into exile in Lingnan, and has already been dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: He has now been sent into exile in Lingnan and is already on his way.

sentences.zh: 乃留其使馬文軌、蔥勿雅，別遣使報之。

translations.literal: He then detained Wuyi's envoys Ma Wengui and Cong Wuya and separately dispatched envoys to report this.
translations.idiomatic: He then detained Wuyi's envoys Ma Wengui and Cong Wuya and sent separate envoys to deliver this reply.

sentences.zh: 俄有泄其事者，武藝又上書云：「大國示人以信，豈有欺誑之理！

translations.literal: Soon someone leaked the matter; Wuyi again submitted a memorial saying: "A great state shows good faith to others—how could there be any reason to deceive!
translations.idiomatic: Before long someone leaked the truth. Wuyi submitted another memorial saying, "A great state shows good faith to others. How could there be any reason to deceive!

sentences.zh: 今聞門藝不向嶺南，伏請依前殺卻。」

translations.literal: Now I hear Menyi did not go to Lingnan; I humbly request that he be killed as before.
translations.idiomatic: I now hear that Menyi did not go to Lingnan. I humbly ask that he be executed as originally requested.

sentences.zh: 由是鴻臚少卿李道邃、源復以不能督察官屬，致有漏泄，左遷道邃爲曹州刺史，復爲澤州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Vice Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial Li Daosui and Yuan Fu, for failing to supervise their subordinates and causing the leak, were demoted—Daosui to Prefect of Caozhou and Fu to Prefect of Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Vice Minister of the Court for State Ceremonial Li Daosui and Yuan Fu were demoted for failing to supervise their subordinates and allowing the leak—Daosui to Prefect of Caozhou and Fu to Prefect of Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 遣門藝暫向嶺南以報之。

translations.literal: Menyi was dispatched temporarily to Lingnan to report this.
translations.idiomatic: Menyi was sent temporarily to Lingnan to satisfy this report.

sentences.zh: 二十年，武藝遣其將張文休率海賊攻登州刺史韋俊。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Wuyi dispatched his general Zhang Wenxiu to lead sea raiders to attack Prefect Wei Jun of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Wuyi dispatched his general Zhang Wenxiu to lead sea raiders in an attack on Prefect Wei Jun of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔遣門藝往幽州徵兵以討之，仍令太僕員外卿金思蘭往新羅發兵以攻其南境。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Menyi to Youzhou to levy troops to suppress them, and further ordered Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud Jin Silan to go to Silla to raise troops and attack their southern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dispatched Menyi to Youzhou to levy troops for the campaign and ordered Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud Jin Silan to go to Silla to raise troops and attack Bohai's southern frontier.

sentences.zh: 屬山阻寒凍，雪深丈余，兵士死者過半，竟無功而還。

translations.literal: As mountains blocked the way and bitter cold froze the land, with snow more than a zhang deep, more than half the soldiers died, and in the end they returned without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains blocked the way, bitter cold set in, and snow lay more than ten feet deep. More than half the soldiers died, and the campaign ended in failure.

sentences.zh: 武藝懷怨不已，密遣使至東都，假刺客刺門藝于天津橋南，門藝格之，不死。

translations.literal: Wuyi nursed resentment without cease, secretly sent envoys to the Eastern Capital, and hired assassins to stab Menyi south of Tianjin Bridge; Menyi parried them and did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi nursed his grievance without cease. He secretly sent envoys to the Eastern Capital to hire assassins to kill Menyi south of Tianjin Bridge. Menyi fought them off and survived.

sentences.zh: 詔河南府捕獲其賊，盡殺之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Henan Prefecture to capture the assassins and kill them all.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Henan Prefecture to capture the assassins and execute them all.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，武藝病卒，其子欽茂嗣立。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year Wuyi died of illness, and his son Qinmao succeeded and was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year Wuyi died of illness, and his son Qinmao succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 詔遣內侍段守簡往冊欽茂爲渤海郡王，仍嗣其父爲左驍衛大將軍、忽汗州都督。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Palace Attendant Duan Shoujian to invest Qinmao as King of Bohai Commandery and again have him succeed his father as Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard and Protector of Hohan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dispatched Palace Attendant Duan Shoujian to invest Qinmao as King of Bohai Commandery and have him succeed his father as Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard and Protector of Hohan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 欽茂承詔赦其境內，遣使隨守簡入朝貢獻。

translations.literal: Qinmao received the edict and proclaimed an amnesty within his borders, and sent envoys following Shoujian to enter court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Qinmao received the edict and proclaimed an amnesty within his borders, then sent envoys to accompany Shoujian to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 大曆二年至十年，或頻遣使來朝，或間歲而至，或歲內二三至者。

translations.literal: From the second to the tenth year of Dali, sometimes envoys were frequently sent to court, sometimes they came every other year, and sometimes two or three times within a single year.
translations.idiomatic: From the second through the tenth year of Dali, they sometimes sent envoys frequently, sometimes came every other year, and sometimes two or three times in a single year.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，遣使獻日本國舞女一十一人及方物。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year envoys were sent presenting eleven dancing girls from Japan and local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year they sent envoys presenting eleven dancing girls from Japan along with local products.

sentences.zh: 四月、十二月，使復來。

translations.literal: In the fourth month and the twelfth month, envoys came again.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth and twelfth months, envoys came again.

sentences.zh: 建中三年五月、貞元七年正月，皆遣使來朝，授其使大常靖爲衛尉卿同正，令還蕃。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Jianzhong and the first month of the seventh year of Zhenyuan, envoys were all sent to court; their envoy Da Changjing was appointed Acting Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and ordered to return to his domain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year of Jianzhong and the first month of the seventh year of Zhenyuan, they sent envoys to court. Their envoy Da Changjing was appointed Acting Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and ordered to return home.

sentences.zh: 八月，其王子大貞翰來朝，請備宿衛。

translations.literal: In the eighth month his prince Da Zhenhan came to court, requesting to serve in the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month his prince Da Zhenhan came to court and requested appointment to the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，以來朝王子大清允爲右衛將軍同正，其下三十餘人，拜官有差。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year, the prince Da Qingyun, who had come to court, was made Acting General of the Right Guard, and more than thirty of his followers below him received offices of varying rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the tenth year, the visiting prince Da Qingyun was appointed Acting General of the Right Guard, and more than thirty of his followers received offices of varying rank.

sentences.zh: 十一年二月，遣內常侍殷志贍冊大嵩璘爲渤海郡王。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eleventh year, Palace Attendant Yin Zhishan was dispatched to invest Da Songlin as King of Bohai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eleventh year, the court dispatched Palace Attendant Yin Zhishan to invest Da Songlin as King of Bohai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 十四年，加銀青光祿大夫、檢校司空，進封渤海國王。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Acting Minister of Works, and further enfeoffed as King of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Acting Minister of Works, and advanced to King of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，遣使來朝。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year envoys were sent to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year they sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 順宗加嵩璘金紫光祿大夫、檢校司空。

translations.literal: Emperor Shunzong promoted Songlin to Golden-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shunzong promoted Songlin to Golden-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 元和元年十月，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Yuanhe, he was further given Acting Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first year of Yuanhe, he was further appointed Acting Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 十二月，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month envoys were sent with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month they sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 四年，以嵩璘男元瑜爲銀青光祿大夫、檢校秘書監、忽汗州都督，依前渤海國王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Songlin's son Yuanyu was made Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Director of the Imperial Library, and Protector of Hohan Prefecture, continuing as before as King of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Songlin's son Yuanyu was appointed Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Director of the Imperial Library, and Protector of Hohan Prefecture, and continued as King of Bohai as before.

sentences.zh: 五年，遣使朝貢者二。

translations.literal: In the fifth year envoys came with tribute twice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year they sent envoys with tribute on two occasions.

sentences.zh: 七年，亦遣使來朝。

translations.literal: In the seventh year envoys were again sent to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year they again sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，授元瑜弟權知國務言義銀青光祿大夫、檢校秘書監、都督、渤海國王，遣內侍李重旻使焉。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year Yuanyu's younger brother, Minister in Charge of State Affairs Yanyi, was invested as Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Director of the Imperial Library, Protector, and King of Bohai, and Palace Attendant Li Chongmin was dispatched on the mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year Yuanyu's younger brother Yanyi, who was managing state affairs, was invested as Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Director of the Imperial Library, Protector, and King of Bohai, and Palace Attendant Li Chongmin was dispatched to carry out the investiture.

sentences.zh: 五年，大仁秀卒，以權知國務大彝震爲銀青光祿大夫、檢校秘書監、都督、渤海國王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Da Renxiu died, and Minister in Charge of State Affairs Da Yizhen was made Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Director of the Imperial Library, Protector, and King of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Da Renxiu died, and Da Yizhen, who was managing state affairs, was appointed Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Director of the Imperial Library, Protector, and King of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 六年，遣王子大明俊等來朝。

translations.literal: In the sixth year princes including Da Mingjun were sent to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year they sent princes including Da Mingjun to court.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，遣同中書右平章事高寶英來謝冊命，仍遣學生三人，隨寶英請赴上都學問。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year Associate Chief Counselor of the Right of the Secretariat Gao Baoying was sent to thank the court for the investiture edict, and three students were also sent with Baoying to request permission to pursue study at the Upper Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year they sent Associate Chief Counselor of the Right Gao Baoying to thank the court for the investiture, and three students accompanied him to request permission to study at the Upper Capital.

sentences.zh: 先遣學生三人，事業稍成，請歸本國，許之。

translations.literal: Previously three students had been sent; when their studies had progressed somewhat, they requested return to their homeland, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Three students had been sent earlier. When their studies had made some progress, they asked to return home, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 二月，王子大先晟等六人來朝。

translations.literal: In the second month six persons including the prince Da Xiansheng came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month six persons including the prince Da Xiansheng came to court.

sentences.zh: 開成後，亦修職貢不絕。

translations.literal: After the Kaicheng era, tribute missions likewise continued without interruption.
translations.idiomatic: After the Kaicheng era, they likewise continued sending tribute without interruption.

sentences.zh: 霫，匈奴之別種也，居於潢水北，亦鮮卑之故地，其國在京師東北五千里。

translations.literal: The Xi were a separate branch of the Xiongnu; they lived north of the Huang River, also in the former Xianbei lands, and their state lay five thousand li northeast of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi were a separate branch of the Xiongnu. They lived north of the Huang River, in the former Xianbei lands, five thousand li northeast of the capital.

sentences.zh: 東接靺鞨，西至突厥，南至契丹，北與烏羅渾接。

translations.literal: East they adjoined the Mohe, west they reached the Turks, south to the Khitan, and north they bordered Wuluohun.
translations.idiomatic: To the east they bordered the Mohe, to the west the Turks, to the south the Khitan, and to the north Wuluohun.

sentences.zh: 地週二千里，四面有山，環繞其境。

translations.literal: Their territory measured two thousand li in circumference; mountains on all four sides encircled their domain.
translations.idiomatic: Their land measured two thousand li around, with mountains on every side enclosing their territory.

sentences.zh: 人多善射獵，好以赤皮爲衣緣，婦人貴銅釧，衣襟上下懸小銅鈴，風俗略與契丹同。

translations.literal: The people were skilled at archery and hunting; they liked to trim their garments with red leather; women prized copper armlets, and small copper bells hung above and below their collars; their customs were broadly similar to those of the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: The people were skilled archers and hunters. They liked to edge their garments with red leather. Women prized copper armlets and hung small copper bells above and below their collars. Their customs were much like those of the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 有都倫紇斤部落四萬戶，勝兵萬餘人。

translations.literal: There was the Dulun Hejin tribe of forty thousand households, with fighting men numbering more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Dulun Hejin tribe numbered forty thousand households, with more than ten thousand fighting men.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，其君長遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan their chieftain sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenguan their chieftain sent envoys with local products as tribute.

sentences.zh: 烏羅渾

translations.literal: Wuluohun
translations.idiomatic: Wuluohun

sentences.zh: 烏羅渾國，蓋後魏之烏洛侯也，今亦謂之烏羅護，其國在京師東北六千三百里，東與靺鞨，西與突厥，南與契丹，北與烏丸接。

translations.literal: The state of Wuluohun was probably the Northern Wei's Wuluohe; today it is also called Wuluohu. Its state lay six thousand three hundred li northeast of the capital; east it bordered the Mohe, west the Turks, south the Khitan, and north the Wuhuan.
translations.idiomatic: The state of Wuluohun was probably the Wuluohe of the Northern Wei; it is also called Wuluohu today. It lay six thousand three hundred li northeast of the capital, bordering the Mohe to the east, the Turks to the west, the Khitan to the south, and the Wuhuan to the north.

sentences.zh: 風俗與靺鞨同。

translations.literal: Its customs were the same as those of the Mohe.
translations.idiomatic: Its customs were the same as those of the Mohe.

sentences.zh: 貞觀六年，其君長遣使獻貂皮焉。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenguan its chieftain sent envoys presenting sable furs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenguan its chieftain sent envoys presenting sable furs.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：北狄密邇中華，侵邊蓋有之矣；

translations.literal: The chronicler states: The Northern Di adjoin China closely, and border raids have surely occurred;
translations.idiomatic: The chronicler writes: The Northern Di lie close to China, and border raids have certainly occurred;

sentences.zh: 東夷隔礙瀛海，作梗罕常聞之。

translations.literal: The Eastern Yi are blocked by the encircling sea, and disturbances are rarely heard of.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Yi are separated by the encircling sea, and trouble from them is seldom heard.

sentences.zh: 非惟勢使之然，抑亦稟於天性。

translations.literal: This is not only because circumstances make it so; it also reflects what is innate in their nature.
translations.idiomatic: This reflects not only the force of circumstance, but also what is born in their nature.

sentences.zh: 太平之人仁，空峒之人武，信矣。

translations.literal: That the people of Taiping are benevolent and the people of Kongtong are martial is indeed true.
translations.idiomatic: That the people of Taiping are humane and the people of Kongtong are martial—it is indeed so.

sentences.zh: 隨煬帝縱欲無厭，興兵遼左，急斂暴欲，由是而起。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang of Sui indulged his desires without end, raised armies in eastern Liaodong, and through urgent levies and violent exactions, turmoil arose from this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang of Sui indulged his desires without limit, raised armies in eastern Liaodong, and through urgent levies and oppressive exactions set the turmoil in motion.

sentences.zh: 亂臣賊子，得以爲資，不戢自焚，遂亡其國。

translations.literal: Rebellious ministers and wicked sons found in this their opportunity; failing to restrain themselves they burned themselves up, and thus their state perished.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellious ministers and wicked sons seized upon this as their opportunity. Unable to restrain themselves, they burned themselves up and thus destroyed their state.

sentences.zh: 我太宗文皇帝親馭戎輅，東征高麗，雖有成功，所損亦甚。

translations.literal: Our Emperor Taizong the Cultured personally drove his war chariot east to campaign against Goguryeo; though he achieved success, the losses were also very great.
translations.idiomatic: Our Emperor Taizong the Cultured personally took the field and marched east against Goguryeo. Though he won success, the cost was also very heavy.

sentences.zh: 及凱還之日，顧謂左右曰：「使朕有魏征在，必無此行矣！」

translations.literal: On the day of triumphant return he turned to those beside him and said, "Had I still had Wei Zheng, I would certainly never have made this expedition!"
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his victorious return he turned to those beside him and said, "If Wei Zheng were still alive, I would never have made this campaign!

sentences.zh: 則是悔于出師也可知矣。

translations.literal: From this one may know that he regretted having taken the field.
translations.idiomatic: From this one may know that he regretted having gone to war.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 夷狄之國，猶石田也，得之無益，失之何傷？

translations.literal: The lands of the barbarians are like stony fields: to gain them is of no benefit, and to lose them—what harm is there?
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian lands are like stony fields: gaining them brings no profit, and losing them—what injury is done?

sentences.zh: 必務求虛名，以勞有用。

translations.literal: Yet one must chase empty renown and thereby wear out what is useful.
translations.idiomatic: Yet one insists on pursuing empty glory and thereby exhausting what is useful.

sentences.zh: 但當修文德以來之，被聲教以服之，擇信臣以撫之，謹邊備以防之，使重譯來庭，航海入貢，茲庶得其道也！

translations.literal: One need only cultivate civil virtue to draw them in, spread cultural instruction to win their submission, choose trustworthy ministers to soothe them, and strengthen frontier defenses to guard against them—so that men passing through many interpreters come to court and ships crossing the sea bring tribute; in this way one may broadly attain the right policy!
translations.idiomatic: One should cultivate civil virtue to draw them in, spread cultural instruction to win their hearts, choose trustworthy ministers to soothe them, and keep frontier defenses strong to guard against them—so that men come to court through many rounds of translation and ships cross the sea bearing tribute. In this way one may broadly attain the right course!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：東夷之人，北狄之俗。

translations.literal: In praise: the people of the Eastern Yi with the customs of the Northern Di.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: the peoples of the Eastern Yi and the customs of the Northern Di.

sentences.zh: 爰考《周官》，是稱蠻服。

translations.literal: Examining the Rites of Zhou, they are called the barbarian domains.
translations.idiomatic: Consult the Rites of Zhou—they are called the barbarian domains.

sentences.zh: 未得無傷，已得何足！

translations.literal: Not to gain them does no harm; once gained, what is there to cherish!
translations.idiomatic: Not gaining them does no harm; once gained, what is there worth keeping!

sentences.zh: 宜務懷柔，謂之羈束。

translations.literal: One should devote oneself to gentle conciliation—this is what is called keeping them on the bridle.
translations.idiomatic: One should devote oneself to gentle conciliation—this is what is called keeping them on the bridle and reins.
